THE UNIVERSITY OF HONG KONG
MEDE4010 Final Year Project
Cheung Hoi Lam
Supervisor: Prof. Barbara Chan
Single Cell Traction Force Measurement Assay with Multiphoton-based Protein Micropatterns
Background
Stem cell therapy is a promising approach for healing many diseases.
In order to improve the efficiency of cell therapy, cell migration process is of interest to understand.
Since cell migration requires the generation of traction force, this project focuses on the improvement and application of traction force assay.
Cellular Functions:
- Cell migration
- Cell shape maintenance
- Cell homeostasis
- Traction Force (TF)
Biological Functions:
- Wound healing
- Morphogenesis
- Metastasis
Existing methods to measure TF:
1. Cell traction force microscopy (CTFM) - unrealistic 2D culture environment
2. Polymethylsiloxane (PDMS) microposts - complicated fabrication process requires additional coating
Multiphoton Fabrication Platform
- 3D soft environment - One step fabrication process
Results
Verification and application
To verify the program, experiments were performed to measure and compare the traction forces of two types of cells - 2D and 3DM cells.
Background of 2D and 3DM cells:
Microsphere encapsulation is a cell delivery platform for stem cell therapy. Cells migrated out of microspheres are called 3DM while cells that remained are called 3DR.
Although no significant difference was found between them, the TF assay was successfully verified with this experiment.
This assay was also applied to study the association between NMII and TF.
Background of Non-muscle Myosin II (NMII):
NMII is a molecule in the cytoskeleton that binds with actin filaments to generate contractile force.
Quantitatively, no relationship was found,
but they exhibited similar patterns on the heatmaps.
TF assay improvements
Best combination of experimental conditions for human mesenchymal stem cell (hMSCs)
passage number 5-7
- Cell seeding density - 500cells/10μl
- Pillar height - 4μm
- Pillar diameter - 1.5μm
- Cell culturing time - 5 hours
Pillar spacing - 1.5μm
A Matlab program was successfully created to analyze the deflected pillar images.
In brief, centroids of each pillar were obtained to find the deflections caused by a single cell.
The values were hence used for calculating cell traction force with a formula.
Conclusion
This project focuses on the improvement and application of traction force assay.
✓ Methodology was refined with the development of a Matlab program
✓ Verified with experiments on 2D and 3DM cells
✓ Applied to study the relationship between NMII and TF
References:
[1] J. H. Wang and J.-S. Lin, "Cell traction force and measurement methods," Biomechanics and modeling in mechanobiology, vol. 6, no. 6, p. 381, 2007.
[2] M. H. Tong et al., "Multiphoton photochemical crosslinking-based fabrication of protein micropatterns with controllable mechanical properties for single cell traction force measurement," Biomedical Optics Express, vol. 9, no. 4, pp. 1853-1867, 2018.
[3] Zhao, B., P. Hu, F.-Y. Yeung, C. Wu, Li, J., Mo, R., Chan, G. C. F. (2015). Self-assembled collagen-human mesenchymal stem cell micropillars for regenerative medicine. Biomaterials, 28(31), 4652-4666.

Group Members: Wenyutian Xu, Tianyi Zhang, Yufu Tao, Ho-Yin Tsang

What is it?
HKU-Denbot is a miniaturized surgical robotic manipulator for future robotic dentistry.
With six Degree-of-Freedom design, the workspace of proposed manipulator could fully cover a human oral cavity dexterously while the whole body could be folded into a 50*50*50 cm³ suitcase, thus it could even be set up in private clinics where the space is severely constrained, especially at large cities like Hong Kong, Tokyo, Singapore and London.
Why Dental robot?
Over half the population in
the world suffer from various oral diseases,
and it will lead to lifelong pain and discomfort.
In developed cities like Hong Kong, there are shortages of medical professionals,
while in rural areas, residents suffer from limited access to healthcare services. Therefore, it is expected HKU Denbot to be the solution for these problems.
System Architecture
Robot Operator (Dentist Master Console)

Design Concept -- Tendon driven
The joints are actuated by steel threads, namely the tendons.
The motors were located outside the manipulator.
Powerful motors can be utilized without affecting the size of manipulator.
The pictures show the arrangements of the tendons. The red lines stand for the tendons. The yellow lines show the tendon sheath, which protect the tendon from scratching against the shell.
Design Concept -- Asymmetry
Shown in figure 1 is the schematic diagram of the manipulator, with D-H parameters indicated.
Table 1 is the D-H table used for forward kinematics analysis.
This design took reference from a human elbow
The workspace (grey area) is only on one side of the arm under asymmetry by inserting spacers (red in Figure 3) to better fit surgical uses.
The maximum "thickness" of the workspace reached 150 mm, well enclosing a human oral cavity. The workspace has been optimized as compared to that of a symmetric configuration (figure 2).
System Analysis
Linear transmission refers to the transmission ratio of the motor angle to the joint angle.
The linearity performance of the first four joints are analyzed.
The results show the the transmission conform to good linear relation
The torque transmission refers to the relationship from motor input torque to joint output torque.
The experimental results showed that it could be approximated as linear system and the payload can successfully hold a dental handpiece

TEXT:
LUMINO
INTRODUCTION
Luminosite is the all-new, innovative navigation solution for the visually impaired.
We hope that our app can be the all-in-one solution for our users.
Luminosite provides accurate, unambiguous instructions to the user via more intuitive means like haptic feedback for a much better navigation experience.
Luminosite integrates the use of the latest technology available like machine learning, augmented reality to provide our users with functionalities current solutions like cane and guidance dog cannot provide: contextualizing surrounding cognition.
We hope this app can be a life changer for the visually impaired and revolutionize how people use navigation apps nowadays, creating a more harmonious, inclusive society for everyone.
FEATURES
Advanced Navigation and Guidance System
Luminosite uses a more direct, intimate way of sensing - haptics. Accompanied by our custom-made navigation instruction algorithm, our haptic enabled guidance system can provide real-time, unambiguous instructions for our users to travel to their destination at ease.
In addition, we have incorporated the latest augmented reality technology - ARKit, to provide an extra layer of safety and accuracy to our users. Taking advantage of the dual camera on the iPhone 7 or later models, with ARKit, we can detect obstacles like walls in the 3D world. Besides, using kinematics information like the users' velocity and acceleration, we can provide warnings to the users in a timely manner and avoiding unwanted accidents.
Latest Machine Learning Technology
Luminosite incorporates the use of machine learning to provide a more comprehensive experience for our users, in particular, machine vision and natural language processing. We use machine vision to help the users with visual disabilities to recognize a wide variety of daily objects in their daily lives. On top of that, we took a step further by providing the relative position of the object to the users, so that they not only know 'what' but also 'where' in front of them.
We also use natural language processing to allow users to operate the application via natural, fluent conversations, just like how we communicate with other humans. Natural language processing analyzes the users' speech as a whole, providing accurate analysis of the users' 'intent' even when the user is speaking casually and not following any predefined format. This enables a smoother learning curve for our users as most of the functions in the app can be achieved by a voice command on top of a visual UI.

FUTURE PLANS
Testing and Evaluation
Even though we have gone through a series of usability testing and acceptance testing on a small group of targeted audience (i.e. around 10 visually impaired users with only 25% to 0% eyesight), we hope that with proper connection and arrangement, we will have the chance to conduct testing on a larger scale in order to receive a greater amount of user opinion input.
Application UI Refinement
Luminosite hopes to develop a new version of the application such that it not only caters the needs of the visually impaired, but also the general public. The idea of providing haptic feedback to the user during the process of navigation is like providing crucial information to the user via the additional sense of feeling. It is different from current solutions which are distracting the users' attention from using their eyesight and hearing to recognize the situation on the road, which can be somewhat dangerous and thus not optimal.

Aim
This project aims to provide an opportunity to explore the field of biomechanics and biomimicry.
Our current objective through this endeavor is to learn about the biomechanics of fish and other underwater organisms. The purpose is to understand how the movements are affected by different variables: speed, turbulence, drag, buoyancy. The model can be applied in surveillance systems and the study of marine biology.
Hardware
RoboFish is controlled by a raspberry pi and powered by a battery.
The raspberry pi sends signals to the DC motor that moves the tail horizontally. However, since the motion of the DC motor is rotational, a mechanism was designed by the mechanical team to translate the rotational motion of the motor to a horizontal motion. In the future, more features such as remote controlling and surveillance systems aim to be added.
Software
Programming language used: C#. Coding in Unity.
Current stage:
Skeleton code for the fish working.
Skeleton code for the controller.
Background research on simulators.
Next stage:
Incorporating a simulator to simulate the environment of the swimming pool (the trial test environment for the model).
Through simulation, variation of different parameters of the fish to analyze which conditions provide best speed and energy efficiency.
Design
The goal is an ideal fish model mechanically designed to possess the following characteristics: Streamlined body. Minimum drag, especially at the edges and in the gaps between separate components. Low weight. Floating stability and buoyancy.
Conclusion and Applications
We believe that there are several applications of our project for research in the academic world. Our model can be used to analyze marine biology through exploration of the sea. A significant possibility is thus the application of surveillance systems, not just in ecosystems research, but also in the navy.

TEXT:
FYP19013: Early Diagnosis of Scoliosis in Children from RGB-D Images Using Deep Learning
Supervisor: Dr. Kenneth K.Y. Wong Second Examiner: Dr. Loretta Y.K. Choi
Team Members: Li Gengyu (3035331886), Huang Siyi (3035335349)
ABSTRACT
Scoliosis is a medical condition where a person's spine has a sideways curve.
It usually occurs before puberty and prevents the lungs from functioning properly in severe cases.
Scoliosis is typically diagnosed from X-ray images, but diagnostic X-rays increase the risk of developmental problems and cancer in those exposed. This project aims to obviate children's X-ray exposure in the early diagnosis of scoliosis by generating X-ray images of children's backs from the corresponding harmless RGB-D images rather than capturing the X-ray images directly from the children.
An RGB-D image of a back combines a standard RGB image with its depth image, and the depth image consists of the distance between each point on the back and the camera to track the spine. In this project, a deep learning model based on HRNet was built and trained to detect landmark locations of the backs on the RGB-D images first.
With the detected landmarks, the X-ray images of the children's backs were eventually synthesized from the corresponding RGB-D images by another deep learning model that was built and trained based on the pix2pix model.
FYP Website:
http://www.comp.hku.hk/fyp/2019-2020/FYP19013
Department of Computer Science The University of Hong Kong
METHODS AND MATERIALS
Data Collection: captured X-ray images and anatomical landmarks with Microsoft Azure Kinect DK from Duchess of Kent Children's Hospital and performed data preprocessing.
Microsoft Azure Kinect DK.
A Sample RGB-D Image with Landmarks.
Landmark Detection: built and trained a deep learning model based on the High-Resolution Net (HRNet) to perform landmark detection on RGB-D images.
The Mechanism of the HRNet:
HRNet: a state-of-the-art deep learning model for landmark detection tasks.
X-ray Synthesis: built and trained a deep learning model based on the pix2pix model to synthesize X-ray images from the RGB-D images and detected landmarks.
The Mechanism of the pix2pix Model:
The pix2pix model: a generative model based on conditional Generative Adversarial Network for image-to-image translation tasks.
INTRODUCTION
This is a deep learning project that aims to synthesize X-ray images of children's backs from the corresponding RGB-D images to eliminate children's radiation exposure in the early diagnosis of scoliosis. This project includes three main phases, data collection, landmark detection, and X-ray synthesis. The main deliverables are two deep learning models based on the HRNet and the pix2pix model for landmark detection and X-ray synthesis, respectively.
Implementation Details
Landmark Detection:
Input: 4-channel RGB-D images.
A Sample RGB-D Image in the Dataset.
Ground Truth & Output: six 1-channel 2D Gaussian heatmaps centered at the landmark locations.
A Sample 2D Gaussian Heatmap.
X-ray Synthesis:
Input: 10-channel RGB-D images with heatmaps centered at the predicted anatomical landmarks (after cropping and resizing).
A Sample Input in the Dataset.
Ground Truth & Output: X-ray images.
A Sample Ground Truth (left) and Output (right).
Results and Analysis
Detected Landmarks:
Analysis: our model can detect the 6 anatomical landmarks accurately on the testing dataset, and the feedbacks from the medical expert were overall positive.
Sample Pairs of Ground Truth (left) and Detected (right) Landmarks.
Synthetic X-ray Images:
Analysis: our model can synthesize relatively clear X-ray images with correct spine curves. The feedbacks from the medical expert were overall positive.
Sample Pairs of Ground Truth (left) and Synthetic (right) X-ray Images.
CONCLUSION
With the two deep learning models for landmark detection and X-ray synthesis based on the HRNet and the pix2pix model, this project achieved its goal of generating X-ray images of children's backs from their corresponding RGB-D images with satisfactory results.

MECH4429 Integrated Capstone Experience
Design, Build and Fly
Summary
With the ever-growing demand for air cargo capacity comes the pursuit for cargo aircraft that combine a large payload with optimum efficiency. The Design, Build and Fly (DBF) team set out to meet this challenge by creating a radio-controlled model airplane, to compete in the Payload Challenge organized by the British Model Flying Association (BMFA). The process involved careful research into aerodynamic engineering and materials science to ensure that the design was sound. The design was proved in test flights by two fully functional prototypes. Various issues were identified during the trials, carefully examined, and subsequently addressed in an iterative process.
The team completely implemented modifications to the design, in an effort to produce the model plane that would carry the target payload with the highest efficiency attainable, and the results hopefully provide useful insights for future model builders and aircraft engineers alike.
Competition Rules
The competition, "Challenge 4 - Quantity" of the Payload Challenge, requires all participating teams to design, construct, and fly an "electric powered, radio controlled aircraft that transport the greatest number of 150 x 7 mm diameter polystyrene spheres with a max. G + / Sg (see Figure 1) along a predetermined course (Figure 2) in the three-minute time slots utilising a pre-determined propulsion unit [1].

Design and Construction
To verify the design concept, the first prototype was designed on a 1:2 scale.
Feedback collected from the first flight test contributed to the modification of the design, leading to a full-scale second prototype fully compliant with the competition requirements.
The design process relied on the use of Computer-Aided Design (CAD) software (Figure 3).
Finite Element Analysis (FEA) was carried out on individual parts to predict their behaviour under load (Figure 4). To ensure high level of precision, construction rigs (Figure 5) and laser-engraved templates (Figure 6) were used.

Technical Specifications and Performance
Two flight tests were carried out on 19 Feb 2020 (1st prototype) and 23 March (2nd prototype) at Hong Kong Model Engineering Club’s (HKMEC) model plane airport in Yuen Long, Hong Kong.
The first prototype crashed immediately after take-off during the first trial. After improvisatory modifications were made on site, the test was able to continue.
The second prototype completed two successful flight cycles justifying the feasibility of the design.
Issues identified were fed into the design of the second prototype. Major improvements included a more streamlined fuselage, larger wings, strengthened landing gear, adjusted motor placement and improved tail shape.
While some issues persisted and new problems were identified, the second prototype was overall a success and ready to be used in the competition.

During the 10 months between July 2019 and April 2020, the team successfully designed, constructed, and flew two prototypes. The final product satisfied most of our initial design objectives.
The team first conducted in-depth research into aerodynamics and aircraft design principles before designing and modifying the plane through an iterative process.
Despite the cancellation of the competition, the project remains valuable as it will offer insights into the aircraft design process for future engineers from the model building community as well as from the industry.

TEXT:
MEASURE
A SenseHat Smart Home Measuring System
LI Ruijie 3035446992
ELEC343 Embedded Systems
Supervisor: Dr. W. L. Tam

Background
Usually, if we would like to measure something at home, there can be some very large professional device, or we can use some small liquid level meter (also known as gradiometer). However, such kind of level meter is not ideal - the precision will be low as you are reading where the bubble is.
Other approaches, like a digital level meter, which can display exact values of the gradient degrees, is not desirable enough due to its high price and difficult operations. So for this project, I am thinking if we can make a digital level meter and something more inside SenseHat to use it, make it intuitive and particularly when we DIY something.
SenseHat is a fascinating piece of hardware. It has all kinds of sensors, and an IMU included. Through reading IMU and other sensors' readings, we can show intuitively on the screen of SenseHat the result we are measuring.

More on IMU
IMU, abbreviation for Inertial Measurement Unit, measures and reports a body's specific force, angular rate, and sometimes the orientation of the body. IMUs are typically used to maneuver aircraft (an attitude and heading reference system), including unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), boats, marine vessels, and spacecraft, including satellites and landers.
An inertial measurement unit works by detecting linear acceleration using one or more accelerometers and rotational rate using one or more gyroscopes. Some also include a magnetometer which is commonly used as a heading sensor. SenseHat has three sensors: one accelerometer, gyro, and magnetometer per axis for each of the three vehicle axes: pitch, roll and yaw. SenseHat uses a library called RTMULib to implement the interface for reading from its IMU.

Function Implementations
Func 1: Digital Level Meter
This function is similar to that offered in iOS's measure app. As there is a tiny gyroscope inside SenseHat, we can read pitch and roll values from the board. When the program detects that roll is between -45° and +45° degrees, the program will switch to pitch measurement mode. In this mode, two circles will be displayed and will turn green if SenseHat is placed horizontally.
When roll is between -45° and 45°, the program will switch to pitch and roll measurement mode. Two circles will be displayed on SenseHat, and they will become circular if pitch and roll approach zero. When zero is reached, the two circles will collapse into one and the display will turn green, meaning that SenseHat lies flat on a surface.
To draw lines programmatically on SenseHat, I have also written a library called sensehat_graphic. The implementation graph looks as follows:

Func 2: Compass & Relative Compass
SenseHat comes with a compass, so we can know which direction is North or South by setting two small dots on the border of the screen. We can also know how many degrees we have turned. By rotating SenseHat clockwise, it will show the degrees increased/decreased. This is also similar to the feature in compass app in iOS. Pressing joystick once, it will set a base yaw value, and then it shows the degrees increased/decreased. Press the joystick again to reset.

Func 3: HomeKit Integration
By installing a tiny server called HomeBridge on Raspberry Pi, we can accept requests from Apple's Home App and send data back to Home App. We can run python scripts to poll from SenseHat's sensors regularly and output the result to HomeBridge.

New Geo-material for Reclamation
Coal Ash-hardened Marine Soil

Background
Extensive sea reclamation are proposed:
• Hong Kong International Airport 3rd Runway System
• Tung Chung New Town Extension
• Lantau Tomorrow Vision
These megaprojects require over 500 million tonnes of fills. However, shortage of backfilling is likely to be a problem.
This study develop a new backfilling geo-material by hardening soft marine deposit primarily with Coal Ash generated from power plants.

Theory
Three ingredients:
1. Coal Ash
2. Cement
3. Marine Soil

Coal Ash and Cement have hydration potential and bind soil particles by filling the voids between soil grains.

Marine soil is soft and often subjected to consolidation settlement. By hardening it, the load bearing capacity increases significantly.
[Coal Ash] + [Marine Soil] + [Cement]
Hardened Specimens
Unconfined compression tests were carried out. The cylindrical specimens were then loaded vertically without confinement.

Introduction>
Our team develops a novel reusable face mask using electrospun nanofibers based filter material. It is expected to partially solve the technical, social and environmental problems related to the current one-time using face masks.
Technique>
Electrospinning is a matured technique to fabricate nanofibers (e.g., dimension at nm level) which are much smaller than the melt-blown fibers (e.g., dimension at μm level) used in the current face masks. The nanofibrinous filter has a high porosity (e.g., > 80%) to allow air filtration with low resistance, meanwhile its large internal surface area enable the great capacity for air pollutants capture. In addition, the electrospinning technique is very flexible to coordinate with other physicochemical approaches to improve the structure and chemistry of the nanofibrinous filters for highly efficient air filtration.
Figure 1. Electrospinning Process
Figure 2. Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM)
Results>
The charts indicate that the nanofibrinous filter has a superior filtration performance with an average removal efficiency of around 90% of 2.5 micrometer particulate matters. And the durability and stability are both much better than the current face masks. It proves that the nanofibrinous filter has much potential to revolutionize the face mask industry.

What is Our Product?
Our product is a 3D-printed Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) with a body design of the iconic Hong Kong trams.
Objective and Target Audience
Our objective is to create a STEM-oriented product that could increase students' interests in the world of robotics, logistics, and automation. FUN FACT:
This is our first hand-drawn sketch of the AGV
Smart Design Feature
Snap-Fit Joints between the Bodies
The snap-fit connections for the main frame/chassis of the bot was adopted to prevent the addition of unnecessary screw holes and made the AGV much lighter and much less complicated. This feature also allows the internal parts of the bot could be easily inspected.
Smart Sensors and Control
Arduino-based Main Control Board
We have incorporated our code into the arduino-based board which is the brains and nerves of this AGV and this has given it its distinctiveness, versatility and functionality. The arduino board is very responsive and can be updated in real time making the software to hardware transfer and integration very effective and smooth.
Ultrasonic Sensor
This component records distance data specified from the bot to the nearest object Advanced versions of these sensors can be implemented in driverless cars and also in factory equipment such as conveyor belts as a future and more industry specific use.
Line Follower
This component uses light sensors to monitor the location of the bot on a given line and update it to the motors in real-time in case some changes to the path need to be made. These can be and are already being used in a much more comprehensive and complex way in the manufacturing and future development of the automotive industry.
Future Design Development

Creating other attractive and iconic designs would increase the students interests toward the product

Installing additional sensor, such as Light or Sound sensors, could increase the complexities and accuracy of the AGV during a task. This is of course would create more challenges for the students.

Keep track of the user's geolocations for facilitating an easy identification of suspected users;
Publish the potentially hazardous areas to the users after analytics of collected data;
Can be used for many times with an appropriate replaceable filter; and
Reduce environmental pollution.
As a result, the proposed smart mask would help building a safe and green community.

SMART DESIGN
The smart mask is washable and reusable for multiple times. Only the replacement of the air filters is required to maintain the best functionality of the air purification. A sensor for measuring the air quality is equipped in the smart mask. Therefore, the user can be notified whenever the quality of air falls below the standard by using a cloud-based platform and a mobile app and thus avoid staying in an environment with stale air. Moreover, the smart mask can be used as a normal mask by removing the sensor part.

WHY IS IT BETTER THAN A REGULAR MASK?
In the past few months, mask waste has been increased, which has resulted in the increase of plastic pollution. However, one of the characteristics of the smart mask is that it can be reused multiple times. They can be washed by water and used for several months. After a few times of use, only the air filters need to be replaced for consistent clean air; but it still contributes tremendously to the environment.

TEXT:
HKU Robomaster
A competition-based platform for innovative young engineers
THE UNIVERSITY OF HONG KONG
HEKUHERCULES
Robomaster is a national robotics competition for university students, hosted by DJH during the summer vacation on a yearly basis.
The path to victory consists of the following steps:
• Form a development team by recruiting technical and managerial members
• Develop a team of auto or semi-auto robots, each with their own functions and restrictions
• Engage in showdowns with other teams of robots. On the battlefield, complete tasks to gain advantage; fire projectiles to lower the HP of enemy robots. A 0HP enemy base is a victory for your team.
HKU Robomaster Team has been recruiting enthusiastic engineering students since 2017.
We aim to cultivate the quality of members that will benefit their career with the practical experience gained during the preparation and participation process.
Our work is divided into technical management, mechanical & hardware management, and software & algorithm development.
The map of Robomaster battlefield
Figure 1. The map of Robomaster battlefield
Mechanical & Hardware designs
The mechanical and hardware design of each robot is based on detailed planning. For each of the robot, we prepared the following technical files before turning concepts into reality:
• Requirement list
• Mechanical layout & actuation plan
• Hardware schematic
The following are the examples of our design. They are:
• Standard (top left): an agile robot on the ground that delivers moderate firepower and smart detection features
• Sentry (top right): a fully auto robot running on a rail near the base. Its firepower is for defense
• Hero (bottom left): a heavy robot dealing the most damage with special projectiles
• Engineer (bottom right): A utility robot that fires, rescues slain robots and delivers special projectiles to the Hero robot
Figure 2. The designs of robots
Technical Management
Technical management is meant to maximize the efficiency of development. It should also regulate the development so that it proceeds in a more orderly way.
The efforts we made this season include:
• Training courses, which offers a set of necessary technical and methodology knowledge.
• Archive system, which governs the naming and organization of development files
• Documentation system, which specifies the technical details that can be referred to during development to minimize confusion.
• Team building activities, like team T-shirt and logo design. These help build the atmosphere in the team and enhance solidarity.
Algorithm development
To ensure victory, it is expected that the robot can be controlled accurately. Smart features like detection and prediction with computer vision are also favorable.
For software and algorithm design, we also come up with detailed plans before development. The plan is known as software structure, which specifies the overall logic and key technical aspects within each step and node. Testing is carried out for fine-tuning.

Swimming across the harbour from Central to TST, our robotic fish will prove its applicability in seawater.
Along with its previous speed record and additional features, it can be beneficial to our society. For instance, its biomimetic nature doesn't interfere with marine life like other underwater vehicles with turbines.
Not only is the new model much more energy efficient, less polluting, but it is also environmentally friendly as it is constructed with less material.
Limitless Underwater Motion Control
• The robot consists of 3 main control protocols: the Roll, Pitch and Yaw.
• We have developed full motion control of the robotic fish with the aid of Motor Feedback system and PID control of the high-torque servo motor. A DIY controller with simply input from joysticks and a potentiometer is developed to provide accurate and quick control of the robot. With the aid of a suitable configuration for our RC set-up, we have achieve a range of 10m for communication.
Professional in manufacturing and waterproofing
• Mimicking a fish-like streamlined shape, the drag from the surrounding water current is reduced.
• With a new, specialized design, we are able to achieve 100% waterproofing with 3D printing only.
• The reinforcement with stainless steel rods has given us sufficient rigidity to overcome the oscillation produced by high-speed travelling.
• The complex bearing system at the tail section has ensured a smooth motion with a very low energy loss.
• From the previous testing, our chassis is certified to be completely waterproofed for at least 24 hours, while also being able to support the fish for a service time of at least 2 months.

Biofilm Inhibition in Oral Pathogens by Nanodiamonds
Principle Investigator: Dr. Zhiqin Chu, Assistant Professor, Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering,
Joint Appointment with School of Biomedical Sciences.
Introduction
Complex microbial communities, e.g., biofilms residing in our oral cavity, have recognized clinical significance, as they are typically the main cause for infections. Diamond nanoparticles, namely, nanodiamonds (NDS) have been demonstrated to work as an effective antibacterial agent against planktonic cells (free-floating state) due to their many promising physico-chemical properties. However, little is known about the behaviors of NDS against biofilms (sessile state).
Novelty of the project
The study revealed for the first time the inhibitory effect on oral pathogenic biofilms by high-quality (ultrapure, robust, biocompatible, and fluorescent) HPHT NDS.
The study uncovered the role of HPHT NDs in inhibiting biofilm formation and their disrupting effect on preformed biofilms in several selected oral microorganisms including fungi (Candida albicans and Candida glabrata) and bacteria (Streptococcus mutans and Porphyromonas gingivalis)
Illustration of experimental design to investigate the effects of NDs on oral pathogens.
The effects of NDS on biofilm formation of C. albicans.

TEXT:
FRing: A Geograph-based P2P Overlay Network for Fast and Robust Blockchain Systems
Haoran Qiu, Tao Ji
Supervised by Dr. Heming Cui
FYP #18006
Department of Computer Science
Faculty of Engineering
Huawei
Background
Features of FRing
FRing addresses the two problems with three features:
Sufficient robustness: a broadcast operation can tolerate at least the same portion of node failure as the blockchain consensus protocol;
Low message redundancy: the messages generated in each broadcast is efficient (O(Ni));
Fast convergence: the convergence time are short enough so that the accumulation of old messages is reduced effectively;
FRing Topology
Conceptually, the network topology of FRING is a self-maintained fractal ring structure, where lower level rings (typically formed by inner-region nodes) reside on higher level rings (typically formed by cross-region nodes) in a recursive way. To form this topology, FRING groups all nodes based on their geographical proximity (per-hop latency) at the bottom level. Each group forms a fully-connected ring. FRING selects multiple nodes from each ring to serve as representatives and they form a new ring in the higher level recursively. Finally, there is only one global ring remaining at the top level and all nodes are connected through representatives.
FRing Architecture
Smart Contract
Cryptocurrency
Blockchain Application
Consensus Protocol
Transactions & Blocks
TxBlock Msg
Blockchain Consensus

FRing Broadcast Mechanism
The broadcast mechanism of FRING is divided into three parts: broadcast up, broadcast down and broadcast within-ring. Broadcast up and down are done with the help of representative nodes. Multiple message paths increase the robustness, which is also parametrized. Broadcast within-ring method is inspired by the distributed k-ary search method which provides O(N) message efficiency. It is done by constructing k-ary spanning trees.
Evaluation Result
We evaluated FRing against Gossip on AWS cloud intensively and evaluation results show that FRing is efficient in terms of both convergence time and message complexity. It is also sufficiently robust for blockchain systems.
Acknowledgements
This project is supported by Huawei Technologies. Firstly, we would like to thank Dr. Cui for his insightful guidance and feedbacks on our project from time to time. We also want to thank Shixiong Zhao, Kusheng Chen, Ji Qi, and Tsz-on Li for their suggestions on improving the work. We are also grateful for our anonymous reviewers for thoughtful feedback, which helped improve the quality of the project, paper, and presentation.
Introduction to FRing
We present FRING, a geography-based P2P overlay network for fast and robust broadcast in blockchain systems. FRING has three main features: sufficient robustness, low message redundancy, and fast convergence. To reduce convergence time, FRING forms the network topology by considering geographical proximity. A novel broadcast algorithm based on FRING topology is proposed to lower message redundancy while maintaining sufficient robustness. This approach eliminates the need for topology inference by traffic pattern analysis. FRING leverages Intel SGX to guarantee nodes' behavior integrity and incorporates pattern obfuscation to prevent the traffic pattern analysis. Evaluation shows that FRing improved the throughput of EOS and Hyperledger Fabric by up to 2.2X and 2.1X respectively.
Research Problems
Recent studies show that the underlying P2P network layer has become the bottleneck for transaction rate. Current blockchain systems form random P2P networks and predominantly use Gossip as the broadcast mechanism for robustness. For each hop in the broadcast process, a node pushes the message to a randomly chosen subset of its neighbors or pull from the message sender. There are two notorious problems associated with this network solution.
1. Gossip generates excessive redundant messages because Gossip is designed for extreme robustness (can tolerate up to 90% node failure). Such redundant messages lead to traffic congestion and low transaction rates.
2. Random network topology causes unnecessarily long broadcast convergence time (i.e., time used for a message to cover all nodes in the network).

Toggle ADHESIVE WI-FI SMART WALL SWITCH ROBOT
Student: Shoyu Kaneko, Hanson Chan
Supervisor: Prof. KS Lui
#1 Smart Feature
#2 Easy Setup
#3 Outdoor Control
Daily Convenience of Smart Light
Initial Inconvenience/ Cost of Installation
IoT Integration w/ RN App & Proximity Sensor
With N-to-1 topology owing to pub/sub pattern in MQTT, multiple applications or devices can trigger Toggle. For the project, React Native (iOS/Android) and a IR Proximity sensor are used.
Mobile App can either toggle real-time or set a weekly routine toggling grid.
IoT IR sensor is also built from Toggle PCB, triggers Toggle when there is an object passed by.
It is demonstrated that the Cloud system built is highly scalable.
HTTPS Microservices on AWS
Mobile App conducts Two Factor Authorization, storing images and setting routines thanks to the microservices built on top of:
AWS Lambda: Function-as-a-service
AWS DynamoDB: NoSQL Database
AWS API Gateway: HTTP API witout CORS
AWS Cognito: User Account system with authenticators
MQTT Broker Sub with AWS IoT (X509 Encryption)
A MQTT broker is hosted on AWS IoT Core. It is secured by TLS/SSL and security tokens, unlike HTTP. MQTT is a bidirectional protocol that provides real-time update of data with very low bandwidth requirement as well as small header size, making it a more reliable IoT protocol even at places with poor connectivity.
Wi-Fi SoC Battery Saving Firmware
ESP8266 Firmware on the Toggle allows OZO monitor and control of wall switches using MQTT on AWS IoT. It has several notable features:
1. Host Captive portal on Access Point for users to select Wi-Fi
2. Receive Flipflop Capacitive Sensor Signals
3. Drive Linear Actuator
4. MQTT Pub/Sub with X509 Security
5. Light Sleep Mode that extends average battery life from 2 days to 20 days
Custom PCB w/ Wi-Fi SoC & LDO
To minimise size and weight of Toggle, custom PCB was designed and fabricated using ESP12S Wi-Fi SoC that has both processor and Wi-Fi Modems. Wi-Fi SoC consumes 3.5mA whereas the ESP8266 consumes 40mA. To reduce input voltage a low dropout voltage regulator (LDO) was used.
Surface mount electronic components are preferred over through-hole components to save more space for the opposite side of the PCB. The PCB size is 27mm*22mm*1.6mm, with HASL finish at a very minimal cost. As the ESP8266 and LDO are both in one package, the PCB acts as multi-purpose IoT platform. For instance, the IoT Proximity sensor device uses the exact same PCB as Toggle.
3D-Printed Linear Actuator
Among all these different mechanisms of linear actuators, Rack-and-pinion with straight gears are used because:
1. Small simple shape (compared to worm gear)
2. Low electrical load (compared to Solenoid)
3. Less fatigue (compared to belt-drive)
OUTCOME
A small, low-cost and 20 days battery adhesive wall switch robot Toggle was built. It runs on a highly scalable AWS microservice system with support for low-bandwidth MQTT protocol. Its unit manufacturing is as low as HKD$30.

Biomedical Engineering
THE UNIVERSITY OF HONG KONG
MEDE4010 Final Year Project
Cheung Hoi Lam
Supervisor: Prof. Barbara Chan
Single Cell Traction Force Measurement Assay with Multiphoton-based Protein Micropatterns
Background
Stem cell therapy is a promising approach for healing many diseases.
In order to improve the efficiency of cell therapy, cell migration process is of interest to understand. Since cell migration requires the generation of traction force, this project focuses on the improvement and application of traction force assay.
Cellular Functions
- Cell migration
- Cell shape maintenance
- Cell homeostasis
Biological Functions
- Wound healing
- Morphogenesis
- Metastasis
Traction Force (TF)
Existing methods to measure TF
1. Cell traction force microscopy (CTFM) - unrealistic 2D culture environment
2. Polymethylsiloxane (PDMS) microposts - complicated fabrication process requires additional coating
Multiphoton Fabrication Platform
- 3D soft environment
- One step fabrication process
Results Verification and application To verify the program, experiments were performed to measure and compare the traction forces of two types of cells - 2D and 3DM cells.
Background of 2D and 3DM cells Microsphere encapsulation is a cell delivery platform for stem cell therapy. Cells migrated out of microspheres are called 3DM while cells that remained are called 3DR.
Although no significant difference was found between them, the TF assay was successfully verified with this experiment.
This assay was also applied to study the association between NMII and TF.
Background of Non-muscle Myosin II (NMII) NMII is a molecule in the cytoskeleton that binds with actin filaments to generate contractile force. Quantitatively, no relationship was found but they exhibited similar patterns on the heatmaps.
Results TF assay improvements Best combination of experimental conditions for human mesenchymal stem cell (hMSCs) passage number 5-7
- Cell seeding density - 500cells/10μl
- Pillar height - 4μm
- Pillar diameter - 1.5μm
- Pillar spacing - 1.5μm
A Matlab program was successfully created to analyze the deflected pillar images. In brief, centroids of each pillar were obtained to find the deflections caused by a single cell. The values were hence used for calculating cell traction force with a formula.
Conclusion This project focuses on the improvement and application of traction force assay.
✓ Methodology was refined with the development of a Matlab program
✓ Verified with experiments on 2D and 3DM cells
✓ Applied to study the relationship between NMII and TF
References [1] J. N. Wang and J.-S. Lin, "Cell traction force and measurement methods," Biomechanics and modeling in mechanobiology, vol. 6, no. 6, p. 361, 2007.
[2] M. H. Tong et al., "Multiphoton photochemical crosslinking-based fabrication of protein micropatterns with controllable mechanical properties for single cell traction force measurement," Biomaterials, vol. 48, pp. 59-68, 2013.

CIVL4102 Project - Tai Ho Ting Louis
The University of Hong Kong Department of Civil Engineering
Identifying Priority Areas for the Improvement of Minibus Service Quality
Introduction
The minibus is the third most popular form of transportation in Hong Kong, contributing 13% of all trips made in the city according to statistics provided by the Transport Department (2014). However, its popularity is still far from the more popular choices, namely rail and franchised bus which contribute 30% and 27% of all trips respectively according to the statistics. Despite that minibus is not the most important form of public transportation, it still has its significance as feeder service which connects local community to major transportation network. Therefore, this project aims to identify the priority areas for improvement of minibus services quality which could serve as a reference for related policy making in the future.
10 Service Aspects Concerned
(1) Service hours (6) Vehicle stability
(2) Route information (7) Safety
(3) Waiting location (8) Reliability
(4) Waiting time (9) Driver's service attitude
(5) Ease of boarding (10) In-vehicle comfort
Data Collection
The primary method for data collection is an on-street questionnaire survey conducted in December 2018 in Hong Kong. 6 student research assistants are kindly recruited by the Department of Civil Engineering of the University of Hong Kong to assist data collection. This survey is conducted primarily based on simple random sampling. The student research assistants approached potential respondents face-to-face and read the questions aloud. The final sample size of the survey is 547, in which 362 are for green minibuses and 185 are for red minibuses.
Ordered Logit Model
The ordered logit model is adopted in this study to investigate the level of contribution of the 10 service aspects individually towards the overall satisfaction level. The model can be expressed in the following formulae.
Yi = 1 if Yi* ≤ k1 (1)
Yi = j if ki ≤ Yi* ≤ ki−1 (2)
Yi = M if Yi* ≥ kM−1 (3)
Yi* = ∑K βkXki + εi (4)
Importance-Satisfaction Analysis
The importance-satisfaction analysis is a key part in this study which aims to identify the priority areas for improvement by studying the combined effect of importance ratings and satisfaction ratings.
Table 1 - Priority for the Improvement of Minibus Service Quality
FOR GREEN MINIBUSES

Group Members: Wenyutian Xu, Tianyi Zhang, Yufu Tao, Ho-Yin Tsang
Supervisor: Dr Z. Wang, PI of Bionics & Control Lab
What is it?
HKU-Denbot is a miniaturized surgical robotic manipulator for future robotic dentistry.
With six Degree-of-Freedom design, the workspace of proposed manipulator could fully cover a human oral cavity dexterously while the whole body could be folded into a 50*50*50 cm³ suitcase, thus it could even be set up in private clinics where the space is severely constrained, especially at large cities like Hong Kong, Tokyo, Singapore and London.
Why Dental robot?
Over half the population in
the world suffer from various oral diseases,
and it will lead to lifelong pain and discomfort.
In developed cities like Hong Kong, there are shortages of medical professionals,
while in rural areas, residents suffer from limited access to healthcare services. Therefore, it is expected HKU Denbot to be the solution for these problems.
System Architecture
Robot Operator (Dentist Master Console)
User Interface (Touch 3D Haptic Device)
Control Program (Application Program Interface)
Robot (HKU-Denbot)
Actuator (High Precision Digital Servo)
Microprocessor (Manipulator Control Board)
Objectives
Compact in Size
6 Degree-of-Freedom Configuration
Optimized Workspace for Dental Surgeries
Design Concept -- Tendon driven
The joints are actuated by steel threads, namely the tendons.
The motors were located outside the manipulator.
Powerful motors can be utilized without affecting the size of manipulator.
The pictures show the arrangements of the tendons. The red lines stand for the tendons. The yellow lines show the tendon sheath, which protect the tendon from scratching against the shell.
Design Concept -- Asymmetry
Shown in figure 1 is the schematic diagram of the manipulator, with D-H parameters indicated.
Table 1 is the D-H table used for forward kinematics analysis.
This design took reference from a human elbow
The workspace (grey area) is only on one side of the arm under asymmetry by inserting spacers (red in Figure 3) to better fit surgical uses.
The maximum "thickness" of the workspace reached 150 mm, well enclosing a human oral cavity. The workspace has been optimized as compared to that of a symmetric configuration (figure 2).
System Analysis
Linear transmission refers to the transmission ratio of the motor angle to the joint angle.
The linearity performance of the first four joints are analyzed.
The results show the the transmission conform to good linear relation
The torque transmission refers to the relationship from motor input torque to joint output torque.
The experimental results showed that it could be approximated as linear system and the payload can successfully hold a dental handpiece

LUMINO
INTRODUCTION
Luminosite is the all-new, innovative navigation solution for the visually impaired.
We hope that our app can be the all-in-one solution for our users.
Luminosite provides accurate, unambiguous instructions to the user via more intuitive means like haptic feedback for a much better navigation experience.
Luminosite integrates the use of the latest technology available like machine learning, augmented reality to provide our users with functionalities current solutions like cane and guidance dog cannot provide: contextualizing surrounding cognition.
We hope this app can be a life changer for the visually impaired and revolutionize how people use navigation apps nowadays, creating a more harmonious, inclusive society for everyone.
FEATURES
Advanced Navigation and Guidance System
Luminosite uses a more direct, intimate way of sensing - haptics. Accompanied by our custom-made navigation instruction algorithm, our haptic enabled guidance system can provide real-time, unambiguous instructions for our users to travel to their destination at ease.
In addition, we have incorporated the latest augmented reality technology - ARKit, to provide an extra layer of safety and accuracy to our users. Taking advantage of the dual camera on the iPhone 7 or later models, with ARKit, we can detect obstacles like walls in the 3D world. Besides, using kinematics information like the users' velocity and acceleration, we can provide warnings to the users in a timely manner and avoiding unwanted accidents.
Latest Machine Learning Technology
Luminosite incorporates the use of machine learning to provide a more comprehensive experience for our users, in particular, machine vision and natural language processing. We use machine vision to help the users with visual disabilities to recognize a wide variety of daily objects in their daily lives. On top of that, we took a step further by providing the relative position of the object to the users, so that they not only know 'what' but also 'where' in front of them.
We also use natural language processing to allow users to operate the application via natural, fluent conversations, just like how we communicate with other humans. Natural language processing analyzes the users' speech as a whole, providing accurate analysis of the users' 'intent' even when the user is speaking casually and not following any predefined format. This enables a smoother learning curve for our users as most of the functions in the app can be achieved by a voice command on top of a visual UI.

RoboFish
Presented by BREED HKU – bio-inspired robotics organization at the University of Hong Kong
Aim
This project aims to provide an opportunity to explore the field of biomechanics and biomimicry.
Our current objective through this endeavor is to learn about the biomechanics of fish and other underwater organisms. The purpose is to understand how the movements are affected by different variables: speed, turbulence, drag, buoyancy. The model can be applied in surveillance systems and the study of marine biology.
Hardware
RoboFish is controlled by a raspberry pi and powered by a battery.
The raspberry pi sends signals to the DC motor that moves the tail horizontally. However, since the motion of the DC motor is rotational, a mechanism was designed by the mechanical team to translate the rotational motion of the motor to a horizontal motion. In the future, more features such as remote controlling and surveillance systems aim to be added.
Software
Programming language used: C#. Coding in Unity.
Current stage:
Skeleton code for the fish working.
Skeleton code for the controller.

TEXT:
FYP19013: Early Diagnosis of Scoliosis in Children from RGB-D Images Using Deep Learning
Supervisor: Dr. Kenneth K.Y. Wong Second Examiner: Dr. Loretta Y.K. Choi
Team Members: Li Gengyu (3035331886), Huang Siyi (3035335349)
ABSTRACT
Scoliosis is a medical condition where a person's spine has a sideways curve.
It usually occurs before puberty and prevents the lungs from functioning properly in severe cases.
Scoliosis is typically diagnosed from X-ray images, but diagnostic X-rays increase the risk of developmental problems and cancer in those exposed. This project aims to obviate children's X-ray exposure in the early diagnosis of scoliosis by generating X-ray images of children's backs from the corresponding harmless RGB-D images rather than capturing the X-ray images directly from the children.
An RGB-D image of a back combines a standard RGB image with its depth image, and the depth image consists of the distance between each point on the back and the camera to track the spine. In this project, a deep learning model based on HRNet was built and trained to detect landmark locations of the backs on the RGB-D images first.
With the detected landmarks, the X-ray images of the children's backs were eventually synthesized from the corresponding RGB-D images by another deep learning model that was built and trained based on the pix2pix model.
FYP Website:
http://www.comp.hku.hk/fyp/2019-2020/FYP19013
Department of Computer Science The University of Hong Kong
METHODS AND MATERIALS
Data Collection: captured X-ray images and anatomical landmarks with Microsoft Azure Kinect DK from Duchess of Kent Children's Hospital and performed data preprocessing.
Microsoft Azure Kinect DK.
A Sample RGB-D Image with Landmarks.
Landmark Detection: built and trained a deep learning model based on the High-Resolution Net (HRNet) to perform landmark detection on RGB-D images.
The Mechanism of the HRNet:
HRNet: a state-of-the-art deep learning model for landmark detection tasks.
X-ray Synthesis: built and trained a deep learning model based on the pix2pix model to synthesize X-ray images from the RGB-D images and detected landmarks.
The Mechanism of the pix2pix Model:
The pix2pix model: a generative model based on conditional Generative Adversarial Network for image-to-image translation tasks.
INTRODUCTION
This is a deep learning project that aims to synthesize X-ray images of children's backs from the corresponding RGB-D images to eliminate children's radiation exposure in the early diagnosis of scoliosis. This project includes three main phases, data collection, landmark detection, and X-ray synthesis. The main deliverables are two deep learning models based on the HRNet and the pix2pix model for landmark detection and X-ray synthesis, respectively.
Implementation Details
Landmark Detection:
Input: 4-channel RGB-D images.
A Sample RGB-D Image in the Dataset.
Ground Truth & Output: six 1-channel 2D Gaussian heatmaps centered at the landmark locations.
A Sample 2D Gaussian Heatmap.
X-ray Synthesis:
Input: 10-channel RGB-D images with heatmaps centered at the predicted anatomical landmarks (after cropping and resizing).
A Sample Input in the Dataset.
Ground Truth & Output: X-ray images.
A Sample Ground Truth (left) and Output (right).
Results and Analysis
Detected Landmarks:
Analysis: our model can detect the 6 anatomical landmarks accurately on the testing dataset, and the feedbacks from the medical expert were overall positive.
Sample Pairs of Ground Truth (left) and Detected (right) Landmarks.
Synthetic X-ray Images:
Analysis: our model can synthesize relatively clear X-ray images with correct spine curves. The feedbacks from the medical expert were overall positive.
Sample Pairs of Ground Truth (left) and Synthetic (right) X-ray Images.
CONCLUSION
With the two deep learning models for landmark detection and X-ray synthesis based on the HRNet and the pix2pix model, this project achieved its goal of generating X-ray images of children's backs from their corresponding RGB-D images with satisfactory results.

Summary
With the ever-growing demand for air cargo capacity comes the pursuit for cargo aircraft that combine a large payload with optimum efficiency. The Design, Build and Fly (DBF) team set out to meet this challenge by creating a radio-controlled model airplane, to compete in the Payload Challenge organized by the British Model Flying Association (BMFA). The process involved careful research into aerodynamic engineering and materials science to ensure that the design was sound. The design was proved in test flights by two fully functional prototypes. Various issues were identified during the trials, carefully examined, and subsequently addressed in an iterative process.
The team completely implemented modifications to the design, in an effort to produce the model plane that would carry the target payload with the highest efficiency attainable, and the results hopefully provide useful insights for future model builders and aircraft engineers alike.
Competition Rules
The competition, "Challenge 4 - Quantity" of the Payload Challenge, requires all participating teams to design, construct, and fly an "electric powered, radio controlled aircraft that transport the greatest number of 150 x 7 mm diameter polystyrene spheres with a max. G + / Sg (see Figure 1) along a predetermined course (Figure 2) in the three-minute time slots utilising a pre-determined propulsion unit [1].

Design and Construction
To verify the design concept, the first prototype was designed on a 1:2 scale.
Feedback collected from the first flight test contributed to the modification of the design, leading to a full-scale second prototype fully compliant with the competition requirements.
The design process relied on the use of Computer-Aided Design (CAD) software (Figure 3).
Finite Element Analysis (FEA) was carried out on individual parts to predict their behaviour under load (Figure 4). To ensure high level of precision, construction rigs (Figure 5) and laser-engraved templates (Figure 6) were used.

Technical Specifications and Performance

MEASURE
A SenseHat Smart Home Measuring System
LI Ruijie 3035446992
ELEC343 Embedded Systems
Supervisor: Dr. W. L. Tam

Background
Usually, if we would like to measure something at home, there can be some very large professional device, or we can use some small liquid level meter (also known as gradiometer). However, such kind of level meter is not ideal - the precision will be low as you are reading where the bubble is.
Other approaches, like a digital level meter, which can display exact values of the gradient degrees, is not desirable enough due to its high price and difficult operations. So for this project, I am thinking if we can make a digital level meter and something more inside SenseHat to use it, make it intuitive and particularly when we DIY something.
SenseHat is a fascinating piece of hardware. It has all kinds of sensors, and an IMU included. Through reading IMU and other sensors' readings, we can show intuitively on the screen of SenseHat the result we are measuring.

More on IMU
IMU, abbreviation for Inertial Measurement Unit, measures and reports a body's specific force, angular rate, and sometimes the orientation of the body. IMUs are typically used to maneuver aircraft (an attitude and heading reference system), including unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), boats, marine vessels, and spacecraft, including satellites and landers.
An inertial measurement unit works by detecting linear acceleration using one or more accelerometers and rotational rate using one or more gyroscopes. Some also include a magnetometer which is commonly used as a heading sensor. SenseHat has three sensors: one accelerometer, gyro, and magnetometer per axis for each of the three vehicle axes: pitch, roll and yaw. SenseHat uses a library called RTMULib to implement the interface for reading from its IMU.

Function Implementations
Func 1: Digital Level Meter
This function is similar to that offered in iOS's measure app. As there is a tiny gyroscope inside SenseHat, we can read pitch and roll values from the board. When the program detects that roll is between -45° and +45° degrees, the program will switch to pitch measurement mode. In this mode, two circles will be displayed and will turn green if SenseHat is placed horizontally.
When roll is between -45° and 45°, the program will switch to pitch and roll measurement mode. Two circles will be displayed on SenseHat, and they will become circular if pitch and roll approach zero. When zero is reached, the two circles will collapse into one and the display will turn green, meaning that SenseHat lies flat on a surface.
To draw lines programmatically on SenseHat, I have also written a library called sensehat_graphic. The implementation graph looks as follows:

Func 2: Compass & Relative Compass
SenseHat comes with a compass, so we can know which direction is North or South by setting two small dots on the border of the screen. We can also know how many degrees we have turned. By rotating SenseHat clockwise, it will show the degrees increased/decreased. This is also similar to the feature in compass app in iOS. Pressing joystick once, it will set a base yaw value, and then it shows the degrees increased/decreased. Press the joystick again to reset.

Func 3: HomeKit Integration
By installing a tiny server called HomeBridge on Raspberry Pi, we can accept requests from Apple's Home App and send data back to Home App. We can run python scripts to poll from SenseHat's sensors regularly and output the result to HomeBridge.

New Geo-material for Reclamation
Coal Ash-hardened Marine Soil

Background
Extensive sea reclamation are proposed:
• Hong Kong International Airport 3rd Runway System
• Tung Chung New Town Extension
• Lantau Tomorrow Vision
These megaprojects require over 500 million tonnes of fills. However, shortage of backfilling is likely to be a problem.
This study develop a new backfilling geo-material by hardening soft marine deposit primarily with Coal Ash generated from power plants.

Theory
Three ingredients:
1. Coal Ash
2. Cement
3. Marine Soil

Coal Ash and Cement have hydration potential and bind soil particles by filling the voids between soil grains.

Marine soil is soft and often subjected to consolidation settlement. By hardening it, the load bearing capacity increases significantly.
[Coal Ash] + [Marine Soil] + [Cement]
Hardened Specimens
Unconfined compression tests were carried out. The cylindrical specimens were then loaded vertically without confinement.

Cement: 5%

No. 1 Malware Vehicle
>60% Email Users
54.6% Spam Email

EXISTING METHOD – BLACKLISTING
This method uses a dataset of blacklisted URLs for prediction.
DRAWBACK: Incorrect for "Zero Day Error"
SOLUTION
Build a new email client.
Read through the contents of email.
Perform analysis on the URLs.
Predict whether malicious or not
IMPLEMENTATION
EMAIL EXTRACTION AND ANALYSIS
"iMap library" was used to login to the email account. Then the URL was extracted from the last unread email. URL based analysis was performed and our optimized model was then run on it.
ARCHITECTURE
The major Python libraries that have been used for this project are:
BEAUTIFULSOUP
SCI-KIT LEARN
TDXTRACT
IMAPLIB
PYTHONSSL
ANALYSIS
URL BASED ANALYSIS
If a URL is split, it reveals different features such as protocol, domain name, etc. Manipulating one or more of these is a strategy often adopted by hackers, and we aimed to combat this.
FEATURE ANALYSIS
We gathered a dataset which had 11000 URLs and their result of being phishing or benign. For each entry, it had 30 features and based on whether the feature was present or absent, a correlation with its result could be obtained.
MACHINE LEARNING
SHORTLISTED MODELS & ACCURACIES
Random Forest had the highest accuracy as compared to the other models and was hence selected.
MODEL
ACCURACY

The use of a Balanced Random Forest

CLASSIFICATION

The web scraper will scrape the email and then run the predictor on it to give the result to the left

Research - Literature Review & Methods like Blacklisting
Solution - Machine Learning applied using URL and feature based analysis
Product - Smart Email Client with 98% accuracy & Webpage

Greater accuracy when training set was changed
Increased efficiency by gradient optimization approach

Introduction>
Our team develops a novel reusable face mask using electrospun nanofibers based filter material. It is expected to partially solve the technical, social and environmental problems related to the current one-time using face masks.
Technique>
Electrospinning is a matured technique to fabricate nanofibers (e.g., dimension at nm level) which are much smaller than the melt-blown fibers (e.g., dimension at μm level) used in the current face masks. The nanofibrinous filter has a high porosity (e.g., > 80%) to allow air filtration with low resistance, meanwhile its large internal surface area enable the great capacity for air pollutants capture. In addition, the electrospinning technique is very flexible to coordinate with other physicochemical approaches to improve the structure and chemistry of the nanofibrinous filters for highly efficient air filtration.
Figure 1. Electrospinning Process
Figure 2. Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM)
Results>
The charts indicate that the nanofibrinous filter has a superior filtration performance with an average removal efficiency of around 90% of 2.5 micrometer particulate matters. And the durability and stability are both much better than the current face masks. It proves that the nanofibrinous filter has much potential to revolutionize the face mask industry.

IMSE2121 - Engineering Training
SMART PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT
Automated Guided Vehicle
What is Our Product?
Our product is a 3D-printed Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) with a body design of the iconic Hong Kong trams.
Objective and Target Audience
Our objective is to create a STEM-oriented product that could increase students' interests in the world of robotics, logistics, and automation. This product is targeted towards Primary and Secondary school educators who need a more fun and approachable way to introduce this technology to the newer generation by combining the design of Hong Kong trams with cultural fun.
Design and Manufacturing of Smart AGV
1. Design Planning and Sketching
2. CAD Modelling using SOLIDWORKS
3. Parts Manufacturing
4. Full Assembly of all parts
FUN FACT:
This is our first hand-drawn sketch of the AGV
Smart Design Feature
Snap-Fit Joints between the Bodies
The snap-fit connections for the main frame/chassis of the bot was adopted to prevent the addition of unnecessary screw holes and made the AGV much lighter and much less complicated. This feature also allows the internal parts of the bot could be easily inspected.
Smart Sensors and Control
Arduino-based Main Control Board
We have incorporated our code into the arduino-based board which is the brains and nerves of this AGV and this has given it its distinctiveness, versatility and functionality. The arduino board is very responsive and can be updated in real time making the software to hardware transfer and integration very effective and smooth.
Ultrasonic Sensor
This component records distance data specified from the bot to the nearest object Advanced versions of these sensors can be implemented in driverless cars and also in factory equipment such as conveyor belts as a future and more industry specific use.
Line Follower
This component uses light sensors to monitor the location of the bot on a given line and update it to the motors in real-time in case some changes to the path need to be made. These can be and are already being used in a much more comprehensive and complex way in the manufacturing and future development of the automotive industry.
Future Design Development
• New Other AGV Design
Creating other attractive and iconic designs would increase the students interests toward the product
• Additional Sensor
Installing additional sensor, such as Light or Sound sensors, could increase the complexities and accuracy of the AGV during a task. This is of course would create more challenges for the students.
• Additional Part
Adding more complex parts, such as an elevated/moving compartment also would increase the difficulties and skills of the AGV.

TEXT:
SMART MASK
Due to the outbreak of COVID-19, a face mask has help us to reduce the spread of the COVID-19 viruses. The use of the mask has been substantially increased. For further enhancing the functionality of the mask, it is desirable for developing a smart product with an integration of digital technologies, including IoT, AI, mobile devices, and cloud computing. The smart product has the following features to minimize the spread of the COVID-19:
Monitor and record the air quality of the surrounding;
Notify users if the surrounding air quality is not acceptable;
Keep track of the user's geolocations for facilitating an easy identification of suspected users;
Publish the potentially hazardous areas to the users after analytics of collected data;
Can be used for many times with an appropriate replaceable filter; and
Reduce environmental pollution.
As a result, the proposed smart mask would help building a safe and green community.

SMART DESIGN
The smart mask is washable and reusable for multiple times. Only the replacement of the air filters is required to maintain the best functionality of the air purification. A sensor for measuring the air quality is equipped in the smart mask. Therefore, the user can be notified whenever the quality of air falls below the standard by using a cloud-based platform and a mobile app and thus avoid staying in an environment with stale air. Moreover, the smart mask can be used as a normal mask by removing the sensor part.

WHY IS IT BETTER THAN A REGULAR MASK?
In the past few months, mask waste has been increased, which has resulted in the increase of plastic pollution. However, one of the characteristics of the smart mask is that it can be reused multiple times. They can be washed by water and used for several months. After a few times of use, only the air filters need to be replaced for consistent clean air; but it still contributes tremendously to the environment.

Microbially Induced Calcite Precipitation (MICP): A Promising Bio-grouting Technique
Bacteria and chemical solution (urea and calcium ions) injected into soil Bacteria hydrolyze urea into carbonate ions [2] CO(NH₂)₂ + 2H₂O → 2NH₄⁺ + CO₃²⁻ Carbonate ions combine with calcium ions to precipitate as calcite in soil pores [2] Ca²⁺ + CO₃²⁻ → CaCO₃(s)
Calcite binds soil grains together, enhancing soil's engineering properties

Calcite content determination Microscopic calcite precipitation patterns

Pure silica sand before MICP treatment
MICP-treated silica sand

Investigate the effects of several influencing factors on the engineering properties of the MICP-treated silica sand Influencing factors: Injected chemical concentration Retention time of injection Relative density Sand particle size distribution Conduct laboratory tests to determine the unconfined compressive strength (UCS) and permeability of the MICP-treated sand

Fire Evacuation Assistance Robot
Ha Ting Pong BEng(EE) II
Ng Ka Chun BEng(EE) III
Hui Chak On BEng(EE) II
Supervisor: Dr. Albert Lee
Dr. Sam K.H. Lam
Introduction
How occupants can evacuate during emergency in High-Rise building has raised different engineer's concern since last century.
The aim of this project is to develop an autonomous robot that assists the emergency evacuation of the disability and injuries in the Temporary Refuse Space and Refuge Floor.
The immediate assistance is a combination of urgent medicine delivery, remotely monitor of patient's status (from face expression judge the urgency) and task assignment from the building management office. The robot is designed to work with other smart cities system like SCADA and Building Management System (BMS) under Artificial Intelligence & Internet of Things Internet Of Thing (AIoT) network, so that the building management can access, monitor, and control the robot from anywhere in the world.
Breadth-First Search
for Shortest Path Travel
The Breadth First Search algorithm is adopted for the robot to desire the path traversal route. A Shortest Path can be found using such algorithm.
AIoT Network for Monitoring, Control,
Face Recognition and Emotion Detection
To allow the user access and control the robot from the Building management firm, a cloud server has been built to host the server for the Node-Red user interface server and the MQTT Broker for IoT protocol. All the sensor data and camera picture gathered from the robot will be sent via MQTT protocol to the cloud server. The cloud server will analysis the data and provide feedback to the user interface.
Networks of the Robot Control
Cargo Delivery and Miscellaneous Functions
Some Additional function like Wireless Charging, Charging Power Monitor, Cargo delivery and Camera Pan Tilt Control are added to accomplish the objective of helping the occupant in refuge floor.
A tailor-made IR light Gate is used to detect if the Cargo are loaded on the robot. Cargo like medicine is proposed to be loaded by the robot and delivery it to the patient.
A wayside robot arm is also proposed to be adopted to transfer the good to the robot. This can be cooperating with other Building Management System (BMS) to accomplish the urgent medicine delivery.

TEXT:
Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering
電機電子工程系
Application of Augmented Reality in Teaching and Learning
Python AR App
- Python Console With AR Output -
Student: Ng Chak Wai
Supervisor: Dr. C.H. Yuen
Abstract
This project is a mobile application that aims to use AR visualization to teach the concept of object and references using some mutable and immutable data types in Python as this is common difficulty for beginner programmers. This app can execute supported Python code and present an AR animation visualizing the underlying concepts. The behavior difference between mutable and immutable data types are shown using their AR models and animations. Sandbox mode and exercise mode are available for user to explore on their own or follow exercises that showcase the properties of the data types. The application is implemented on the iOS platform using RealityKit and the Vision framework. While the application is adequate for learning the basic concept, the support set of operation can be expand in the future for a more complete coverage.
Methodology
To illustrate the idea of objects and references, for each operation, a memory table will be printed in AR to show what the operation is doing. The operation is animated as the Memory table changes. For Lists, multiple List variables, as arrows, may point to the same location at the memory table, where as non-mutable types such as Tuple will be shown as a taped cardboard box that does not share its location with anyone.
Modes of Operation
Input: Python Code
Output: AR Animation of the Execution
Sandbox Mode
- Scan any supported code for execution
- Works on printed text on paper or text on monitor
- Behaves just like Python
Exercise Mode
- Execute code from a file designed to showcase the property of the data types
- Guide the user to explore in the right direction
Variable Explorer
- Do read operations directly on variables
- Also shows behavior of subscripts
- Scans and tracks printed labels
Conclusion
As technology gets incorporated into the classroom, there is more research on what can be used to enhance the learning experience. Using AR in education is beneficial to students' motivation to explore and help them come up with new hypotheses. It is suitable for learning conceptual ideas.
The application aims to teach the relationship between the data and the operations for mutable and immutable types in Python using AR. Through executing supported Python code, the user is able to explore the properties of the variables. The visualization of these properties is enhanced with the use or AR.
Objects of different types are given different AR models, and behave according to their behavior in Python. The user is able to scan their own input or use input from exercise mode. User can also see mutable values with explorer mode in a more interactive way.
- Limitations: Limited Supported Operations
The application does not support all operations or data types in Python. Even for the supported data types, not all built-in methods are supported. It would be beneficial to show which methods are mutating.
- Limitations: Limited Interactivity
The scanning and execution of code are separated, and the user does not interact with the AR scene physically once the animation begin. The core function of the application can be improved in terms of interactivity, for example with markers that respond instantly.
