TEXT:
Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering
電機電子工程系
Game App for Pick and Place 3D Printed Robotic Arm
Student Name: Yip Wai Sheung
Supervisor: Dr.T.W Chm
Abstract
This project proposed to build up a "Compact AlphaGo" which may contribute a new idea for the implementation of an intelligent chess game. An Android chess game application was developed by Flutter with a Flask image processing server which was developed by Python.
The Minimax Algorithm and Alpha-Beta Pruning constructed a "brain" to the AI which is embedded inside the Android app. For the current status, the AI can only foresee 3 steps. A more intelligent algorithm is needed for future development. Also, image processing was time-consuming; some unnecessary procedures on image processing can be trimmed to speed up efficiency.
For the hardware part, a robotic arm with a chess stacker was built by the 3D modeling software AutoCAD. The cheesses were programmed in a way that they could be placed only on certain grid of the chessboard. But the cheesses can't be placed at the center of the grid. Therefore, using a magnetic chessboard and cheesses is recommended.
Methodology
The whole system workflow was simple. It was planned to use a mobile phone, which has two Uis: one for the camera preview and another one for virtual chessboard, to capture an image of the chessboard. The image processing procedures were supposed to run within the mobile phone but finally decided to build a Python server to do the image processing in the cloud. After the image processing come up with a result that all the cheesses on the chessboard have been located with a unique grid index. Then the system can base on the location of the cheesses to calculate the probability for each chess and choose the most probable one to win the chess game. After that, the command will be sent by g-code to the Arduino Mega board, then it can base on the position information from the encoder engine of each stepper motor to control the robotic arm grasp a chess to the grid that was decided by the algorithm.
Image Processing System
A Go/king chess game must include 3 items: a chessboard, white cheesses and black cheesses. By following the computer science problem solving steps, these three items should be counted as three subproblems which are needed to be processed separately. The figure 1, figure 2 and figure 3 show the details of how to process these three items
Robotic Arm Design
The robotic arm was made by assembled all the 3D printed components of the robotic arm. The geometry structure and kinematic algorithm were contributed by Florin Tobler [1], who is a member of the open-source community GitHub. The robotic arm has a vacuum gripper with a self-made chess stacker for automatic chess grasping
Minimax Algorithm with Alpha-Beta Pruning
Minimax Algorithm will traverse the tree for the best result which the result is the leaves of the tree. Then backtrack to the root, finally, the algorithm will choose the path which can arrive the end node or visit the child node, which is along with the path, as the next chess move.
The score sheet shown below is for Maximizer; for the Minimizer, all of the score become negative value, and the Minimizer will calculate the sum of all negative score to achieve a minimum value. Each score item shown in the table representing a specific situation of chess pattern.
Result
After around 100 times of experience under the condition of yellow light bulb illumination, the accuracy of chessboard and cheesses detection can be up to over 95%. Under flash light illumination, the accuracy of cheesses detection decreases to around 80%. There are no machine learning approaches involved, so the accuracy of the image processing is totally depending on the RGB value of the cheesses and chessboard.
As can be seen from the benchmark of the Minimax Algorithm before and after optimization below, the efficiency of the chess game AI is impressively improved. But the algorithm still can't foresee three or more moves. This improvement is due to the reduction of branching factor and the depth of the minimax tree
Conclusion
The whole project was completed, and all the objectives were achieved eventually, and the experimental result has mentioned.
Some optimization can be done for both software and hardware area in this project. For the software problem, the algorithm efficiency still needs to be improved by some heuristic. To improve the win probability of the AI, some machine learning approaches can be used. The image processing part is still not as intelligent as I thought, which the accuracy under different environment conditions can be improved by implementing the machine learning algorithm, or simply use K-means as I mentioned before.
For the hardware problem, it's suggested to use end-stop which may probably improve the accuracy of motor control. Also, a quite simple way to place the chess to the center of the grid, the magnetic cheesses and chessboard can be used.

TEXT:
Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering
電機電子工程系
Drawing Robot and Selfie Smart Phone App
Student: CHEUNG Kai Sum
Supervisors: Dr. T.W. Chim Mr. David Lee
Abstract
In subtractive manufacturing technology, the CNC (Computer Numerical Control) machine is used widely.
The drawing robot has a similar mechanism as the conventional one can be used by the user to draw the image they want. The main task of this project is developing an Android app and algorithm for transforming the image to a G-Code file. Also solving the unbalance problem and end-stop button installing.
In this project, the app was developed using Android Studio which included the Bluetooth Module, Camera Module, Image Processing Module and other necessary modules in order to achieve the main function.
The balance problem was fixed in the project by designing a supporter to make the pen holder can move horizontally and the End-stop buttons were installed with "Homing Cycle" and "Return" operation. There are two transform methods for users to do processing in different conditions.
All basic functions have been completed at the end of the project include the app building and hardware improvement. The future development is making drawing robots can draw on various platforms by fixing pen holder supporter. Also, the software can run with other image processing algorithms to overcome the environmental factor by dealing with the image with Computer Vision technology.
Methodology
The drawing robot contains two main components which are Android app operation and image processing.
The "Drawing Robot Controller" app includes Bluetooth communication function and image transform function. The user can choose a device from the Device Choosing page and then click on the image to be transformed into G-Code file, and send it to the robot. From the received G-Code, the robot can analyze G-Code and make an action.
For transforming function is used to convert the raster image into vector image with G-Code algorithm. The app can read the G-Code sequence and send it to the drawing robot controller.
One-Line Image Transformation
As shown in Figure 1, there are four stages of transformation. The original image should change into a grayscale image first. Secondly, using the "Floyd-Steinberg Algorithm in Error Diffusion" to change the image into a binary image. Thirdly, the user can choose the transform method which is either one-adapting elit or two-adapting elit, and so on.
Original Image
Grayscale Image
G-Code File (Drawing Result)
Binary Image
Sketch Version Image Transformation
From Figure 2, there are two main methods used in this method which are Gaussian Blur and dodging images. As showing in the black graph, a Gray Scale image should be prepared first. Then the Gray Scale image is blurred with Gaussian Blur function to get a smooth image. Finally, it's dodged with the grayscale image with proper degree blur.
Original Image
Gray Scale Image
Gaussian Blur Image
Dodging Images
Result
Figure 3: Drawing Robot Controller App (Main Pages)
The "Drawing Robot Controller" app combines the controlling function and image transform function. From Figure 3, paired devices can be chosen from the Device Choosing page and there are two control methods for users to do processing in different conditions.
Figure 4: Drawing Result of Image Transformation Algorithms
From observation in Figure 4, the drawing result of "One-Line Image Transform" is darker than the original image. However, the algorithm can present all details in the image. The result with "Sketch Version Image Transformation" expresses more details and clearer image. The characters can be shown more clearly in the result but some details will be eliminated as it is a sketch.
Project Summary
Our project mainly focuses on developing a mobile app that can control the drawing robot and doing the image transform function. The main contribution of this project is to make the robot hold the pen stably. To solve the first limitation needs machine learning and computer vision techniques to reduce the environmental influence. For holders, it can be added other running motor and fixed 3D model for stable drawing.

OBJECTIVES
Minimally invasive surgery (MIS), despite various advantages, heightens operational complexity. Here, we present an augmented reality(AR) application that reduces such complication by anatomic hologram overlay. Incorporating a novel triplet calibration algorithm, this app can achieve accurate registration much faster than current strategies. Installed with line-drawing and demonstration functions, this app provides assistance throughout pre-, intra- and post-operative scenarios. With SURGVIEW, we hope to develop a more intuitive and interactive future of clinical practices, with specific focus on head-and-neck surgeries.
BACKGROUND
Current AR applications have two major limitations:
Time-consuming and inaccurate spatial registration:
Manual: perceptive distortion
Point-based: time-consuming and human error
Marker-based: automatic but unstable
Singular intra-operative functionality
Extended application in pre- and post-operative scenarios;
DISTINGUISHED FEATURES
The application developed has two distinguished features comparing to currently available solutions:
Triplet Calibration Algorithm:
Marker-based CV detection;
Total registration time ≤ 8sec;
Mean re-projection error (RPE) 4.27mm;
Multi-Functionality:
Hologram-attached pre-op time marker;
Manipulatable anatomic structure;
Shared view among calibrated HoloLens;

TEXT:
Smart Water Auditing using IoT, and Machine Learning – Dashboard
Student name: Henry Lui
Supervisor: Dr Edith Ngai
Abstract
As an aim of the Smart Water Auditing Project is to increase participants' water usage awareness, a dashboard was designed to be an simple yet reliable device for users to view their water usage statistics. This involves designing an intuitive graphical user interface to visualise users' water statics in a simple manner, as well as designing a communications system for the dashboard to retrieve up-to-date data to be shown on the graphical user interface.
Dashboard Overview
While the graphical user interface visualises data for users, the Wi-Fi module connects the dashboard to the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) server via Wi-Fi where data is retrieved. Meanwhile, the microcontroller is responsible for processing data received by the Wi-Fi module and displaying it on the graphical user interface which is displayed on the dashboard's screen.
Graphical User Interface Layout
1. Daily Stats
This tab allows users to easily review their daily water consumption.
2. Monthly Stats
This tab shows the monthly water usage.
3. Settings
The dashboard's configurations can be found in this tab.
Communications
The dashboard connects to a database by connecting to an MQTT broker via Wi-Fi where it retrieves data to be updated on the graphical user interface. The figure below illustrates how this is achieved.

TEXT:
Cake decoration with 3D printer
Padmanabhan Kishoth/Lui Wing Ming/Tam Ho Kai/Tam Chun Fai/ Ng Hon Fai
Supervisor: Dr M.M.Y. Choy
Department of Mechanical Engineering

INTRODUCTION
• Cake decoration is an art which can take many years to perfect, even for a professional pastry chef.
• 3D printer technology is a novel creative solution to help bakers master cake decorating skill.
• Advantages over the traditional approach include speed and accuracy, so that complex design can be more easily achieved.
• This study aims to modify an existing 3D printer to make it compatible to extrude food material to decorate the top and side walls of a Cake.

METHODS
• A Rheometer is used to measure the fluid properties and analyse compound chocolate and Nutella for decorating.
• An extruder is a component on 3D printer that ejects out materials. Modified extruders are used in form of Syringe paste extruder which prints 2D edible food paste.
• Hot melt extruder to print 3D edible chocolate models.

RESULTS
• Results reveal that paste extruder can successfully print simple to complicated designs using both Nutella and chocolate icing on the top surface of the cake.
• Hot-melt extruder can print 3D compound chocolate using dark and milk chocolate models to decorate both the top and side wall of cake.
• Combining both one can achieve in decorating the top and sidewall of the cake which could be potential in usage in baking quicker, tasty and more complicated designs for amateur bakers and pastry chefs

ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS
• We would like to express our thanks to our teachers, Dr Marian Choy, Ms Mable Choi and Dr Match Ko for their continuous support and encouragement.
• We would like to express our gratitude towards Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing members in supporting our project and organising 6th Inno Show 2022.

TEXT:
Pick and Place Game App for 3D Printed Robotic Arm
Team member: Wong Ka Ngai, Benny Wan Tsun Wai, Alan
Supervisors: Dr. T. W. Chim, Mr. David Lee
Introduction
This project aims at developing a Connect Four AI for STEM education that utilizes a mobile application and a robotic arm to play with human opponents. It is hoped that students' interest in CS and AI can be aroused by playing with the product.
Hardware
The robotic arm has a servo gripper that picks from the self-made disc stacker and places in the board. End-stops are installed for auto-homing and the Bluetooth module allows the app to instruct the robotic arm.
Components
RAMP14, Arduino MEGA 2560, SPP-CA, Servo motor, Stepper motors x3, end-stop switches x3
Robotic arm
Project setup
System Overview
Control Robotic Arm to place disc
Send G-code
Connect 4 Game App
developed in android studio
Firebase
"Post" Player Score To Firebase
"Get" Player Scores From Firebase Database
Access camera and capture image
OpenCV
JNI with CMake
AI algorithm in C++
Load
Transposition Table
Return next move
Find next move
Board Detection
The app uses OpenCV to detect the board. It captures and preprocesses the empty board images, then utilizes circle detection algorithm (Hough Circle Transform) to find the 42 circular slots. After getting the center coordinates of the 42 circles, HSV color detection identifies their change of colors, checking for teal or pink disc.
Connect 4 AI
The unbeatable AI is made using a minimax algorithm with Alpha-Beta pruning. Given a Connect 4 state, it traverses a tree with all possible future states. Tree leaves are the terminal states and their values are returned to the root. During search, some branches are cut off as a better move is available. The algorithm chooses the move that can arrive the optimal leaf. Besides playing optimally, the AI tells player the remaining steps to lose and gives hint.

TEXT:
WE HUNT, WE EXPLORE, WE THRIVE WITH OUR BEST FRIEND: DOGS, SINCE THE DAWN OF HUMANITY.
Like dogs, quadruped robots are envisioned to play an inseparable part in urban operations under the new normal. DoggiE aims to become the first industrial-grade quadruped robot developed by HKU, accomplish accolades of the quadruped robot "Spot" at Boston Dynamics, and supplement task forces during emergencies and shortage of manpower, broadening the range of surveillance and minimizing injuries/damage to human resources.
ADVANTAGES OF DOGGIE
Unique combination of strength and agility
Accompaniment of robustness with capacity
Platform for implementing complex solutions
Friendly incorporation into the community
MANUFACTURING
The latest prototype is 40x20x40mm in size and weighs 1kg. The model comprises a main body framework for accommodating electrical/battery components and 4 legs, each of 3 limbs and 5 joints.
A hybrid model of manufacturing was utilized for optimal robustness and weight.
3D parts such as limbs were modelled in SolidWorks and printed with Polymaker PolyLite material
Part of the body framework comprises Laser cut acrylic sections
A total of 12 Goosky DSSEERVO DS3218MG 20kg Metal Gear Digital Steering Servos are used for the 4 limbs
IMPLEMENTATION OF IOT
The ESP32 module is used as the microcontroller unit, as it contains an embedded Bluetooth module capable of initializing a BLE server and detecting Bluetooth clients (i.e. Mobile devices with our DoggiE application)
The inertial measurement unit (IMU) comprises the Adafruit LIS3MDL+ISM330DHX feathering, which collects and feeds rotational and positional data into the control system
Simulations were run on the PyBullet physics engine for proof-of-concept of both our backend algorithms (e.g. Walking and auto-balancing) and validation of our mechanical design
FEATURES OF CURRENT PROTOTYPE
WALKING, SITTING, STRETCHING
DoggiE enjoys a wide range of motion, which enables it to perform complex tasks while maintaining balance.
REMOTE APP CONTROL
DoggiE is fully responsive to mobile control and implements the latest IoT technology by utilizing BLE networks.
REAL-TIME USER FEEDBACK
DoggiE transmits data in real-time and allows users to monitor information retrieved from DoggiE, including its current status (e.g. rotation and position).

TEXT:
Soft Body Manipulation with Differentiable Physics
Chen Sirui, Liu Yun Hao, Yao Shang Wen
Supervisor: Dr. Pan Jia
Goal
Apply Differentiable Physics to enhance Deformable Objects Manipulation
TL;DR: Help robot play with clay by understanding physics!
Challenge
1. Curse of dimensionality + complicated dynamics of deformation => Encoder/Decoder structure with trajectory reconstruction loss
2. Embedding simulation into deep learning requires the simulator to be end-to-end differentiable => Customize from open-sourced differentiable simulator Plasticinelab
Simulator Architecture
A simulator that supports articulated robot system with collision detection and differentiable forward kinematics and soft body with differentiable elasticity and plasticity is put together in the project. The renderer is built in an event-driven fashion.
DiffSRL Network Design
Trajectory reconstruction loss with differentiable simulator allow soft body dynamics to be backpropagated to Autoencoder.
PlasticineLab Benchmark
Comparing to other representation learning methods, DiffSRL achieves the state-of-the-art performance across all soft body manipulation tasks in Plasticinelab.
Task Fulfillment Keyframes
DiffSRL is able to produce visually similar result in simulator and real world.

TEXT:
COMP3329 Computer Game Design and Programming
Uni Fighters
大學街大龍門
Knock your rivals out the U-Street!
Uni Fighters is a game that we have made for the course COMP3329 - Computer Game Design and Programming. It is a 2.5D fighter game set at the University of Hong Kong, portraying a student who gets into a fight for bumping into his schoolmate. Players will play as a student to fight against the opponent using combat mechanics. The game is made with the goal of acting as a stress reliever for players, as well as providing a medium to explore the campus of the University of Hong Kong.
Fully Custom Made Models and Assets
We made all models and assets from scratch, including the characters, maps, shaders and particle effects.
Meet Sami and Carol, our original game characters! We modelled and handpainted our custom characters in Blender. Every part of them, including the scarf and the hood, are fully sculpted by us from scratch.
By referencing pictures online and captured by ourselves, we modelled a 1:1 replica of the HKU's U-Street in Blender. We applied royalty-free textures including wood and bricks to make it look more realistic.
With the Unity's default shader, the characters looked bland and plastic-like. Using Unity's URP Shader Graph, we made and applied our custom cel shader to the characters to make them look cartoon-ish and lively.
We added particle effects on impact, such as when the characters are being hit by their opponents and when they land on the ground. They were all made from scratch using Blender and Unity's VFX graph.

Introduction & Story
FOOD CITY PANDA Run! is a 3D Runner Game developed during the course of COMP3329 Computer Game Design and Programming. The game idea is actually drawn from a book-keeping app called Fortune City which applies gamification of personal finance managing. We aim to apply a similar design to food delivery apps such as foodpanda, that the game can be embedded to those apps to meet business objectives as retain current customers and attract new ones.
The background story goes as follows. In 20 AC (After Covid), Hong Kong is under a great depression of economy and food supply. To make ends meet, the player has to take a part-time job as a food delivery guy. However, in today's world, even the slightest mistake can lead people being fired, to make sure all the food reaches their customers intact, the player must avoid all obstacles appearing on their road of delivery...
Technical Specifications and Assets Used
FOOD CITY PANDA Run! is developed on Unity game engine and used c# as scripting language. All assets were purchased on unity asset store, including Hong Kong Street (for overall game scenes), Japanese School Lunch (for food choices), and Mobile Traffic System (for player car). For sound effect of the game, such as background music and coin collect effects, we referred to some online open source of audio materials. Some sample game scenes and assets are shown below:
Player View of Roads, coins and Obstacles
Player Car with Food
Road Barrier as Obstacle
Game Logic
1. The player initially has 3 food on the tray for delivery.
2. The player can move Left or Right by pressing ← and →, or A and D, to avoid hitting the obstacles and to collect coins as delivery tips.
3. If the player have a minor or indirect collision (like pushing) with the obstacle, it will push the obstacle away without punishment.
4. The food will drop from the tray if the player hit directly with the obstacle. The number of food that drops depends on how hard the player hit the obstacle.
5. The player fails the game if there is no food left on the tray.

TEXT:
HINCare: An Intelligent Timebanking System for Elderly Care
Team Member: Hu Zhenwei
Supervisor: Prof. Reynold Cheng
In Hong Kong, the number of elderly citizens is estimated to rise to 1/3 of the population (8.27 million) in year 2037.
As they age and become more frail, the demand for support services (e.g., providing domestic or escort services) will increase significantly in the coming years.
However, there is a severe lack of manpower to meet this demand due to the aging workforce and shortage of employees. There is thus a strong need of voluntary or part-time helpers for taking care of elders.
HINCare is now downloadable in Apple and Google Play Store; it has been serving more than 2000 elders and helpers in NGOs (e.g., SKH and CSFC).
The app is designed with large fonts and spacing for the ease of elder users. The system attracted media attention, and won the Asia Smart App Award 2020 - Merit Award and the Faculty of Engineering Community Investment and Inclusion Fund (CIF), a government funding agency and its associated NGOs in 2021.
We introduce HINCare, an app that encourages mutual-help in the community. HINCare adopts the concept of timebanking, where each user has his/her own account to store the amount of time ("time credits"). Users can exchange these "time credits" with other users for providing and receiving services or other services.
Moreover, HINCare uses HIN (Heterogeneous Information Network) to recommend helpers to elders. HIN is a huge graph which stores the relationship information among elders, helpers, and NGOs. We use HIN to match elders and helpers by calculating the similarity between them. Our team uses HINs and AI technologies for matching elders and helpers. It is based on our recent research results.
HINCare is a cloud-based system. Administrators of elderly care centers use the system through a convenient web-based interface to perform daily tasks (e.g., user registration, event announcement, and user profile management), etc. The system has a simple and easy-to-use interface, and the system is easy to learn and use.
The system is generic and flexible, allowing NGOs to join our scheme easily.
AI Recommendation of Volunteers
Use: of HIN Algorithm to recommend suitable volunteers to the service requesters
Real-time Web Portal Monitoring
Together with the mobile App, NGO's Staff can monitor and follow up with the volunteering Services Progress, enhancing work efficiency
Time Credit Account Review
Reward Redemption
NGOs can use the statistic analysis to better plan and organize the resources to serve the community, compiling reports
We adopt HIN (Heterogeneous Information Network) in our project to facilitate the recommendation process.
We then utilize fine-tuned TransT (Translating Embeddings for Modeling Multi-relational Data). We also use other models such as BiRc, Top-pop. TransT performs the actual recommendations. HR (Hit Ratio) and NDCG (Discounted Cumulative Gain) are used as the metrics for measuring model accuracy.

TEXT:
HKU iGEM 2022
AMPed
Problem
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a phenomenon arising from the indiscriminate use of antibiotics and other antimicrobial compounds. Harmful microbes acquire resistance genes that grant them immunity when exposed to antimicrobials. This has led to the concerning emergence of drug resistant bacteria or "superbugs". The WHO declared AMR to be in the "top 10 global public health threats facing humanity".
However, the risk from this menacing phenomenon is not restricted to human health. It is a threat to the environment and environment-dependent industries such as the food industry, which predicts massive production, economic losses, and food safety concerns.
The effects of AMR can be observed on a local scale as well within the Pearl River Delta. In Hong Kong, resistance surveillance in food done between December 2019 and June 2020 revealed that out of the 851 raw beef, chicken, and pork samples tested, 30.1% tested positive for resistant strains. Similarly, out of the 304 samples of vegetable salad, salmon sashimi, and tuna sashimi tested, 15.1% were positive for resistant strains.
AMPed - Our Solution
Antimicrobial Peptides (AMPs)
Addressing the challenge of superbugs and meeting the demand for alternatives are a class of compounds called Antimicrobial Peptides (AMPs). AMPs are innate defense proteins that have broad-spectrum antimicrobial with high targeting specificity, due to their ability to distinguish pathogenic cell membranes from host cell membranes. Most importantly AMPs are significantly more difficult to develop resistance towards. Our AMP of interest Cecropin B hails from the Cecropia moth and has proven to be highly and broadly effective against microbial pathogens
Microalgae
To complement our powerful AMP, our chassis of choice eventually led to Chlorella vulgaris var. autotrophica. Its low susceptibility to AMPs and efficient expression of complex proteins made it an ideal chassis for the expression of Cecropin B. Compounding Chlorella's known high growth rate, low maintenance cost and straightforward culturing as well as a high nutritional value to the consuming species, it has potential for application as a fish feed supplement in aquaculture, agriculture and even human consumption.
Two-Pronged Application
AMPed integrates Cecropin B and Chlorella into two potent applications: The Secretion Model uses Chlorella as a protein factory, producing Cecropin B in high quantities to be purified for a multitude of downstream uses. The Encapsulation Model takes advantage of the nutrition and robustness of Chlorella to carry Cecropin B internally as a capsule which can convey passive immunity through a supplement or feed product.
Expansion plans
While project can be expanded with little effort and minimal financial strain, there is still work to be done. The completed product needs extensive laboratory testing to ensure maximal nutritional value and antimicrobial effect. The production pipeline needs to be streamlined to ensure fast and efficient manufacturing. Field trials also need to be conducted to witness the Chlorella in action in a real world setting so that inputs can be obtained from end users to make final adjustments to suit the needs of the consumers. The project must be also scaled up to industrial levels to meet demands from the markets.

generation OF ROBOTICS.

Objectives
• Enhance manoeuvrability to navigate through real-world terrains
• Improve waterproofing technique for continuous deployment in water bodies
• Increase robustness and efficiency of mechanical/electrical system
• Increase controllability by providing better user experience
Swimming across the harbour from Central to TST, our robotic fish will prove its applicability in seawater.
Along with its previous speed record and additional features, it can be beneficial to our society. For instance, its biomimetic nature doesn't interfere with marine life like other underwater vehicles with turbines.
Not only is the new model much more energy efficient, less polluting, but it is also environmentally friendly as it is constructed with less material.
Limitless Underwater Motion Control
• The robot consists of 3 main control protocols: the Roll, Pitch and Yaw.
• We have developed full motion control of the robotic fish with the aid of Motor Feedback system and PID control of the high-torque servo motor. A DIY controller with simply input from joysticks and a potentiometer is developed to provide accurate and quick control of the robot. With the aid of a suitable configuration for our RC set-up, we have achieve a range of 10m for communication.
Professional in manufacturing and waterproofing
• Mimicking a fish-like streamlined shape, the drag from the surrounding water current is reduced.
• With a new, specialized design, we are able to achieve 100% waterproofing with 3D printing only.
• The reinforcement with stainless steel rods has given us sufficient rigidity to overcome the oscillation produced by high-speed travelling.
• The complex bearing system at the tail section has ensured a smooth motion with a very low energy loss.
• From the previous testing, our chassis is certified to be completely waterproofed for at least 24 hours, while also being able to support the fish for a service time of at least 2 months.

Supervisor: Dr. H.H. Cheung
Project Background
Lagori, the theme of ABU Robocon 2022, is an ancient Indian game that involves Seeker Robot stacking the Lagori Tower and Hitter Robot interrupting opponent's Seeker by attacking its Ball-on-Head.
Project Objectives
To inspire students to design and manufacture robots in an innovative way
To develop students' sense of teamwork and innovation
To provide opportunities for exchanging knowledge and visiting other colleges through local and international contests
R1 "HITTER"
Auto Aiming Camera
Using depth camera to detect sphere shaped objects within line of sight, and predict position of opponents' ball-on-head.
3-BELTS SHOOTER
Three long angled belt providing a stable exit velocity and spin for the hitter ball. Ensuring consistency and fast exit velocity.
PNEUMATIC BALL MAGAZINE
Balls loading and feeding mechanism actuated by pneumatic cylinders.
SUSPENSION MODULE
Spring dampers for ensuring the largest contact surface area between the balls and the belts at any location inside the barrel
R2 "SEEKER"
Pneumatics Ball Gripper
Gripping mechanism with just one actuator, reducing both weight, cost and complexity.
CHASSIS TRAJECTORY AUTOMATION
Trajectory generated with cubic spline allows the robot to move along the fastest path. With the usage of Encoders and Gyroscope, the robot could follow the generated trajectory accurately.
BALL-ON-HEAD BALANCER
An active evading mechanism for dodging opponents' hitter robots' attack.
ACTIVE CASTER CHASSIS
Using separate motors for steering and propulsion to get double the acceleration over typical maximum chassis with less occupied space and lower weight.

Robocon HONG KONG 2022
3 point gripper combined with a belt system to transport and stack the lagori pile in high speed.

First Prize Project
RoboMaster Sim2Real 2022 Challenge
About the project
RoboMaster Sim2Real Challenge is a robotic competition in which each team designs algorithms for an AI-driven confrontational robot to accomplish two tasks:
1. activate five target objects in the battle field
2. fight with an enemy robot.
Participants are allowed to conduct experiments in a simulator, while direct access to the real-world robot is forbidden. The submitted algorithms of a team will be deployed for real-world validation by the organizers, which determines the final rank.
Our project combines various task-specifically optimized robotic algorithms with some typical confrontation strategies, and achieved an impressive performance.
Localization
Our localization method is based on Lidar map matching. The robot will consistently receive Lidar signal of the surroundings, and then use it to locate itself on a static map.
Navigation
A refined A* algorithm is used for path planning and path tracking. When a path is found by A*, we translate it into a series of smooth (cubic) curve and further adjust the speed of turning points w.r.t. the robots physical kinetic parameters.
Decision-Making
Initially, we attempted to explore the possibility of bringing Reinforced Learning to generate actions for the robots. However, due to the complicated confrontational environment and limited resources, we at last chose to use the decision tree. We set up a series of rules for the robot to make decisions, and at each step it will filter out less beneficial points according to the rules.

3DuPrint
HKU 3D PRINTING CLOUD SUBMISSION SYSTEM
PROJECT BACKGROUND
The print jobs to 3D printers in HKU are handled manually by making a schedule in the booking system, instead of a cloud 3D print submission system.
The project aims to maximize the efficiency of printing new jobs, and make it easier for students and teachers to submit jobs to HKU's 3D printers by automating the process of submitting new jobs.
Simplifies job submissions by auto-filled forms
PRINT JOB APPROVAL SYSTEM
A print job approval system can reject invalid or bad prints from users. Users will receive an email about the changes requested without approaching the site, increasing the efficiency of submitting new jobs.
AUTO-SCHEDULING SYSTEM AND REMOTE PRINTING
3DuPrint will use the estimated print time obtained from auto-slicing print jobs and schedule jobs to the available printers. The schedule system can be further extended to send jobs to 3D printers remotely and automatically.
TECHNOLOGIES & FRAMEWORKS USED
3DuPrint is mostly written in TypeScript and consists of two parts: Front-end and Back-end. The front-end is written using React, Prisma and GraphQL are used to facilitate the communication to the back-end. For the back-end, MariaDB (a better MySQL) is used to store print job records. Docker is used to launch the servers without any hassles.

SIMULATION AND BIG DATA ANALYTICS FOR ON-DEMAND RIDE-HAILING SERVICES
Department of Civil Engineering
The University of Hong Kong
Background and Motivation
1. Smart Mobility is set out as one of the smart area by the HK Gov.
in the Smart City Blueprint.
2. Emergence of ride-hailing services are seen as a revolutionary while disruptive change to the industry.
3. Regulations on taxis and ride-hailing services in Hong Kong are seen to be outdated and falling behind.
Policy 1: Increasing Cap of Passengers
Results from survey study:
• High demand for larger taxis in terms of seating capacity and trunk size
• Current saloon taxis cannot carry large group of passengers or large luggage
• Not economical, inefficient, inconvenience, and sometimes problematic & dangerous
• Suprisingly high demand for wheelchair accessible taxis despite low percentage of respondents are disabled
• Current saloon taxis are inaccessible for wheelchair
Implementation of this policy:
• Force new MPV taxis to install ramps and harnesses
• Allow higher flag down fare for MPV taxis
• Higher fare incentivise the change of fleet vehicles
• Economical for passenger travelling in large group, but more expensive if travelling individually
• Better allocation of limited resources
Saloon taxis will have to change into MPV taxis if cap is increased to 6 person
Policy 2: Dynamic Pricing Mechanism
Results from simulation platform:
• The best pricing rule is a 5% price increase at all high demand periods
• Results showed that compared to a fixed price mechanism, dynamic pricing can:
- Increases income for drivers
- Increases utilization rate
- Improves matching rate
- Improves in service provided (in terms of waiting time)
Implementation of this policy:
• Rides that starts at high demand periods would be subject to a 5% increase in fare at the end of the journey
• High demand periods set as: 7-9am, 5-7pm.
• Price increases are not recommended to be imposed at midnights and early hours
- Deemed unreasonable as there are limited alternative transportation choices
- Seems like forcing the passengers to pay a higher price
- Easy and simple to implement
Policy 3: Fleet Optimisation
Results from simulation platform:
• The best fleet size is 2 taxis per 1000 population
• Results showed that compared to the current fleet size (2.4 taxis per 1000 population), the new fleet size can:
- Increases income for drivers
- Increases utilization rate
- Improves matching rate
- Worsen in service provided (in terms of waiting time)
Implementation of this policy:
• Taxi licenses must be purchased back by the government
• Extremely difficult and costly to implement
• Would not be a cost effective policy
Author: Mak Kam Ho
This project is made possible with the help of Smart Mobility Lab at HKU
For more details, please visit: https://sites.google.com/view/keintao

BARTENDER

Nowadays, applications of robotic automation have started to take place in different industries and fields of work, especially in the food and beverage industry. In this project, we are going to perform a bartending job and produce a cocktail automatically with a robotic arm, OpenMANIPULATOR-P.

OPENMANIPULATOR-P
OpenMANIPULATOR-P is a robotic arm with 6 joints, hence 6 degrees of freedom. Each joint can turn 180 degrees. It can reach a maximum of 767.3 mm (including gripper) and is capable to handle 3 kg payload. A python program was written with Moveit! commands to plan and execute the robotic arm's movements so that it can perform bartending tasks.

LAYOUT DESIGN
We have built a one wall layer design with three-sided walls. Open ceiling on the top, in case of the collision between the walls and the arm. Alcohol bottles are placed on the outer part of the wall. Holes are cut on the walls for arm's moving in and out through the holes for bartending and serving job. A wooden bottom plate is also included for consolidating the whole placement design and preventing the collapse of the equipment and frame.

GRAPHICAL USER INTERFACE
A graphical user interface (GUI) was designed to enhance the ergonomics of our product, makes the interaction between humans and computers simple.

HKU Robomaster
A competition-based platform for innovative young engineers
THE UNIVERSITY OF HONG KONG
HKSU HERCULES
Robomaster is a national robotics competition for university students, hosted by DJH during the summer vacation on a yearly basis.
The path to victory consists of the following steps:
• Form a development team by recruiting technical and managerial members
• Develop a team of auto or semi-auto robots, each with their own functions and restrictions
• Engage in showdowns with other teams of robots. On the battlefield, complete tasks to gain advantage; fire projectiles to lower the HP of enemy robots. A 0HP enemy base is a victory for your team.
HKU Robomaster Team has been recruiting enthusiastic engineering students since 2017.
We aim to cultivate the quality of members that will benefit their career with the practical experience gained during the preparation and participation process.
Our work is divided into technical management, mechanical & hardware management, and software & algorithm development.
The map of Robomaster battlefield
Figure 1. The map of Robomaster battlefield
Mechanical & Hardware designs
The mechanical and hardware design of each robot is based on detailed planning. For each of the robot, we prepared the following technical files before turning concepts into reality:
• Requirement list
• Mechanical layout & actuation plan
• Hardware schematic
The following are the examples of our design. They are:
• Standard (top left): an agile robot on the ground that delivers moderate firepower and smart detection features
• Sentry (top right): a fully auto robot running on a rail near the base. Its firepower is for defense
• Hero (bottom left): a heavy robot dealing the most damage with special projectiles
• Engineer (bottom right): A utility robot that fires, rescues slain robots and delivers special projectiles to the Hero robot
Figure 2. The designs of robots
Technical Management
Technical management is meant to maximize the efficiency of development. It should also regulate the development so that it proceeds in a more orderly way.
The efforts we made this season include:
• Training courses, which offers a set of necessary technical and methodology knowledge
• Archive system, which governs the naming and organization of development files
• Documentation system, which specifies the technical details that can be referred to during development to minimize confusion
• Team building activities, like team T-shirt and logo design. These help build the atmosphere in the team and enhance solidarity.
Algorithm development
To ensure victory, it is expected that the robot can be controlled accurately. Smart features like detection and prediction with computer vision are also favorable.
For software and algorithm design, we also come up with detailed plans before development. The plan is known as software structure, which specifies the overall logic and key technical aspects within each step and node. Testing is carried out for fine-tuning

TEXT:
HKU IGEM 2023
LEAPS
"LOCAL ENVIRONMENT ALLIANCE"
PROJECT SERIES
# INTRODUCTION
Hong Kong is a bustling metropolis with over 7 millions citizens. With its dense population and rapid economic growth, the city is facing a number of pressing environmental challenges that threaten the health of its citizens and the ecosystem. Given the versatility and precision of synthetic biology, it carries many potentials in dealing with environmental issues with high efficiency and small/no negative environmental impact. "LEAPS" is a project series now consists of two subprojects, each tackling a different aspect of existing environmental challenges. With the achievement and success from the finished AMPed project, we now continue on our B-MAT system.
# FINISHED SUBPROJECT: AMPed
The project lacked the aquatic aspect of the local environment. The emphasis was on the Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) which is a phenomenon in which harmful microbes acquire genes resistant to antimicrobials. The effect of AMR has been observed in the local Pearl River Delta region. The fish industry is meanwhile heavily influenced by AMR as microscopic pests that infect fish can not be countered by conventional means.
The solution provided is the transgenic AMP-expressing microalgae fish feed supplement, that delivers passive immunity and nutrition to fish in aqua systems plagued with AMR. In the project, our team focused on the expression and production of Cecropin B (CecB) in the microalgal chassis Chlorella vulgaris var. autotrophica (Chlorella). CecB is an antimicrobial peptide(AMP) found in the Cecropia Moth (Echelona biosciences, 2022), with innate broad-spectrum antimicrobial activities and rare intervals of resistance. We introduced it to the pisciculture industry via a fish feed supplement by designing two forms of products – the AMP isolate powder and the microalgae protein with the AMP encapsulated.
The quality, mainly referring to the stability and toxicity, of the products was examined. The result is that not only CecB has high stability to pH and temperature but also it imposes no threats to health. Finally, the AMPed can be utilized by all farmers in the pisciculture industry and even amateur breeders with aquarium fishes.
# UPCOMING SUBPROJECT: B-MAT SYSTEM
Problem:
Battery recycling in Hong Kong has gained increasing attention during rapid industrial development. Currently, the two mainstream methods to recycle rechargeable batteries - hydrometallurgy and pyrometallurgy both come with negative environmental impacts. As an alternative, bioleaching is a recycling method that uses microbes to recover useful metals in batteries in a cost-effective and eco-friendly way. But current practice of bioleaching exhibits two main problems: (1) Slow reaction kinetics, (2) Bacteria have low tolerance towards oxidative stress, hindering the scalability of the technology.
Solution:
Hence, in this project, we propose a novel bioleaching system for lithium ion battery recycling using genetic engineered A. thiooxidans.
We plan to:
1.design genetic circuit / overexpress genes (e.g. Sox, Hdr)
2.modify regulator in the A. thiooxidans genome (e.g., MerR/MgA // add Glutathione - Metal resistance/ Anti-Oxidative Stress)
Then the bioleaching process will be carried out in a two-stage method.
(I)In the first bioreactor, our modified A. thiooxidans will be cultured under suitable conditions.
(II)The bacteria will be pumped to the second bioreactor to react with lithium waste paste. After the bioleaching in the second bioreactor, our product is extracted through a valve and the recovery process is continued.
Future plan:
Apart from A.thiooxidans, we are looking for other bacteria that possess similar function (e.g., Pseudomonas) to further improve the leaching performance. And with a higher recovery rate and lower cost for battery recycling, we are considering extending the recycling to printed circuit boards or electronic waste in Hong Kong. Since the components in these wasted products are similar to batteries, bioleaching will also have a promising effect on their recycling.

TEXT:
SLAM Robot with monocular depth estimation in application
Student name: Tam Yung Yip Supervisor: Dr. C.K. Lee
Abstract SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) technology, which combines mapping with robot localization[1], can help solve the problem of developing accurate environmental maps for robots in unfamiliar environment. This project aims to construct a robot using SLAM and a monocular camera for depth estimation.
PID control on the car base control
The PID method, which stands for proportional, integral, and derivative, will be utilized to minimize mistakes in motor speed control. Proportional gain shortens the control system's reaction time, but if it is set too high, the system may become unstable. Integral gain can be aggregated with each speed increase to reduce steady-state inaccuracy. Derivative gain is used to use system stress and can dampen the system. The PID algorithm combines these three parameters to provide fast, accurate, and consistent outcomes.
SLAM method
It is an estimation methods of the distribution of robot pose, the uncertainty of robot pose will increase while robot moving. The error can be reduced by the measurement update through recursively using the getting encoder and map data by sensors. The equation of the robot pose will be:
p(x_{t+1},m|z_{V_t},u_{V_t})
U-Net structure of monocular depth estimation
The U-Net model is commonly utilized in computer vision tasks for depth estimation. It obtains the contour of the picture by extracting features from two same-size upsampling and downsampling layers, which is then processed through the network's encoder and decoder sections with the ReLu activation function[2]. The U-Net model takes a single RGB picture as input and returns a depth map that represents the distance between items in the scene and the camera. It extracts features using convolutional layers and reconstructs the depth map using deconvolutional layers while maintaining spatial information and incorporates global context.
Result
Able to do mapping with path-planning without any labelling And output 3D point cloud depth image

TEXT:
IEEE ICRA AI Challenge 2020
Supervisor:Dr. Jia Pan, Assistant Professor, Department of Computer Science
Student Representatives:Tingxiang Fan, Sirui Chen, Jialong Li, Chuek Yin Chui
Introduction
ICRA AI Challenge is a worldwide college students robotics challenge held by IEEE Robotics and Automation society and DJI.
Each team represents a university which need to program two purely automatic robots and compete with other teams in a RTS game manner. Deep learning and other AI related technology will be used. The challenge will be divide into three sub-topics: Decision making; Perception and Navigation.
Navigation
To make our robot more agile in planning as well as deal with narrow space and dynamic obstacles we implemented a parallel heuristics based rapid exploring random tree (RRT*) algorithm in cooperate with Local Reciprocal Velocity Obstacle multiagent collision free policy.
Decision Making
We uses behavior tree for decision making, compared with FSM and decision tree, this approach can support realtime decision making as well as making the code portable
Diagram for Behavior Tree
Perception
We design an efficient object detection and tracking algorithm combining kernalized correlation filter tracker and SVM+ HOG detector as well as parallel programming logic. The tracking pipeline can be run at 140 FPS, which significantly boost up the system response.
Conclusion
We ranked 10th over 80+ international teams and won the excellent prize in robot navigation algorithm design competition. All the members involved has got hand on experience of doing large scale programming project and learnt how to work in a team with git.
For technical part, since this year's competition has been moved online, the practical testing regarding some algorithms robustness is still undetermined, which will be implemented and tested next year. Moreover, the decision making pipeline currently is not scalable to more complex tasks, which remains to be optimized next year.

- A playful way to learning AI and robotics -
WOO Chung Yu, NG Ka Lok, YIP Tsz Fung, CHEN Wu Juang, CHING King Him, LI Jason Chun Lok
INTRODUCTION
Research works in deep reinforcement learning have been emerging, however, only few of them actually demonstrate results on real physical agents. Duckietown Project provides an opportunity to properly benchmark the current state of the art of these methods as applied to real robotics system. The mission of our project is to democratise Artificial Intelligence (AI) and robotics research. Through this project, students gain tangible experience in a fun way in assembling self-driving robots and applying AI to the physical education platform developed by MIT.

TEXT:
IEEE ICRA AI Challenge 2020
Supervisor:Dr. Jia Pan, Assistant Professor, Department of Computer Science
Student Representatives:Tingxiang Fan, Sirui Chen, Jialong Li, Chuek Yin Chui
Introduction
ICRA AI Challenge is a worldwide college students robotics challenge held by IEEE Robotics and Automation society and DJI.
Each team represents a university which need to program two purely automatic robots and compete with other teams in a RTS game manner. Deep learning and other AI related technology will be used. The challenge will be divide into three sub-topics: Decision making; Perception and Navigation.
Navigation
To make our robot more agile in planning as well as deal with narrow space and dynamic obstacles we implemented a parallel heuristics based rapid exploring random tree (RRT*) algorithm in cooperate with Local Reciprocal Velocity Obstacle multiagent collision free policy.
Decision Making
We uses behavior tree for decision making, compared with FSM and decision tree, this approach can support realtime decision making as well as making the code portable
Diagram for Behavior Tree
Perception
We design an efficient object detection and tracking algorithm combining kernalized correlation filter tracker and SVM+ HOG detector as well as parallel programming logic. The tracking pipeline can be run at 140 FPS, which significantly boost up the system response.
Conclusion
We ranked 10th over 80+ international teams and won the excellent prize in robot navigation algorithm design competition. All the members involved has got hand on experience of doing large scale programming project and learnt how to work in a team with git.
For technical part, since this year's competition has been moved online, the practical testing regarding some algorithms robustness is still undetermined, which will be implemented and tested next year. Moreover, the decision making pipeline currently is not scalable to more complex tasks, which remains to be optimized next year.

TEXT:
A Robotic Catheter System for MRI-guided Cardiac Electrophysiological Intervention
Ziyang Dong1, Ziyuan Guo1, Denny K.C. Fu1, Kit-Hang Lee1, Martin C.W. Leong1,
Chim Lee Cheung1, Wayne Luk2, Fellow, IEEE, Ka-Wai Kwok1
1 Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Hong Kong
2 Department of Computing, Imperial College London
APTORUM SIGNATE
Index Terms – Cardiac Electrophysiology, MR-safe Robot, Robot-assisted Intervention, MR-safe Actuation

Background
Motivation:
EP catheterization is an effective treatment for heart rhythm disorders, in which a catheter has to perform radiofrequency ablation (RFA) in the heart chamber (Fig.1);
Intra-operative MRI provides superior soft tissue contrast [1], which helps to access the lesion locations and ablation progress (Fig.2), so as to guide the catheter;
Robot can improve the accuracy of catheter manipulation for intra-cardiac EP intervention. Tele-operation of robot also eliminates the need of screens in MRI room.
Challenges:
Difficult to control the long (1.5m) and flexible EP catheter under the influence of beating heart chamber;
No ferromagnetic materials are allowed in MRI.

Method
Main features of the robotic catheter system:
Master-slave hydraulic actuation with low-friction rolling diaphragm seals are used to achieve MR-safe and precise actuation (Fig.4c & d);
All components of the robot slave part are made of MR-safe material and hydraulically actuated to minimize the EM interference; Catheter tip can be located by MR-based positional tracking in real-time to close the control loop (Fig.4a).
(a) Position tracking coil
(b) Long (1.5m), flexible catheter
(c) Slave part
(d) Master actuation units
Tubes for hydraulic transmission (~10m)
Electric motors
Rotation
Bending
Insertion
Control room
Long (1.5m), flexible catheter
Gears and shafts
Fig.4. Catheter robot platform incorporated with a standard EP catheter. The master-slave actuation units enable rotation, bending and insertion of the catheter. Two tiny coils are for real-time positional MR-tracking [2].
Fig.4a. Position tracking coil
Fig.4b. Long (1.5m), flexible catheter
Fig.4c. Slave part
Fig.4d. Master actuation units

Results
Experimental validation:
MRI-compatibility test: Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) loss <2%. Image artifact was negligible even when the robot is in motion (Fig.5);
Lab-based pulmonary vein isolation task: The teleoperated robot demonstrated high precision and sufficient workspace to create target lesions with an EP catheter (Fig.6).
(a) Experimental setup of MR-compatibility test of the presented robot. The operator can tele-manipulate the catheter using the navigation interface [3].
(b) MR images of an MRI phantom placed aside the robot.
(c) LA model
(d) Target lesion path
(e) Front view showing the catheter tip footprint, the 30 targeted "lesion" points, and also the desired lesion targets (yellow).
(f) Side views showing the catheter tip footprint, the 30 targeted "lesion" points, and also the desired lesion targets (yellow).

Conclusion
The proposed MR-safe catheter robotic platform offers dexterous tele-manipulation of a cardiac catheter under intra-op MRI guidance. The high-efficient hydraulic transmission using rolling-diaphragm has demonstrated great potential of offering rapid but precise actuation under MRI, without adversely affecting the imaging quality.
References: [1] Nazarian et al., Circulation, 2008; [2] Cheung, C.L., et al., Hamlyn Symposium on Medical Robotics, 2016; [3] Lee, et al., Transactions on Mechatronics, 2018.

A Robotic Catheter System for MRI-guided Cardiac Electrophysiological Intervention
Ziyang Dong1, Ziyuan Guo1, Denny K.C. Fu1, Kit-Hang Lee1, Martin C.W. Leong1,
Chim Lee Cheung1, Wayne Luk2, Fellow, IEEE, Ka-Wai Kwok1
1 Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Hong Kong
2 Department of Computing, Imperial College London
APTORUM SIGNATE
Index Terms – Cardiac Electrophysiology, MR-safe Robot, Robot-assisted Intervention, MR-safe Actuation

Background
Motivation:
EP catheterization is an effective treatment for heart rhythm disorders, in which a catheter has to perform radiofrequency ablation (RFA) in the heart chamber (Fig.1);
Intra-operative MRI provides superior soft tissue contrast [1], which helps to access the lesion locations and ablation progress (Fig.2), so as to guide the catheter;
Robot can improve the accuracy of catheter manipulation for intra-cardiac EP intervention. Tele-operation of robot also eliminates the need of screens in MRI room.
Challenges:
Difficult to control the long (1.5m) and flexible EP catheter under the influence of beating heart chamber;
No ferromagnetic materials are allowed in MRI.

Method
Main features of the robotic catheter system:
Master-slave hydraulic actuation with low-friction rolling diaphragm seals are used to achieve MR-safe and precise actuation (Fig.4c & d);
All components of the robot slave part are made of MR-safe material and hydraulically actuated to minimize the EM interference; Catheter tip can be located by MR-based positional tracking in real-time to close the control loop (Fig.4a).
(a) Position tracking coil
(b) Long (1.5m), flexible catheter
(c) Slave part
(d) Master actuation units
Tubes for hydraulic transmission (~10m)
Electric motors
Rotation
Bending
Insertion
Control room
Long (1.5m), flexible catheter
Gears and shafts
Fig.4. Catheter robot platform incorporated with a standard EP catheter. The master-slave actuation units enable rotation, bending and insertion of the catheter. Two tiny coils are for real-time positional MR-tracking [2].
Fig.4a. Position tracking coil
Fig.4b. Long (1.5m), flexible catheter
Fig.4c. Slave part
Fig.4d. Master actuation units

Results
Experimental validation:
MRI-compatibility test: Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) loss <2%. Image artifact was negligible even when the robot is in motion (Fig.5);
Lab-based pulmonary vein isolation task: The teleoperated robot demonstrated high precision and sufficient workspace to create target lesions with an EP catheter (Fig.6).
(a) Experimental setup of MR-compatibility test of the presented robot. The operator can tele-manipulate the catheter using the navigation interface [3].
(b) MR images of an MRI phantom placed aside the robot.
(c) LA model
(d) Target lesion path
(e) Front view showing the catheter tip footprint, the 30 targeted "lesion" points, and also the desired lesion targets (yellow).
(f) Side views showing the catheter tip footprint, the 30 targeted "lesion" points, and also the desired lesion targets (yellow).

Conclusion
The proposed MR-safe catheter robotic platform offers dexterous tele-manipulation of a cardiac catheter under intra-op MRI guidance. The high-efficient hydraulic transmission using rolling-diaphragm has demonstrated great potential of offering rapid but precise actuation under MRI, without adversely affecting the imaging quality.
References: [1] Nazarian et al., Circulation, 2008; [2] Cheung, C.L., et al., Hamlyn Symposium on Medical Robotics, 2016; [3] Lee, et al., Transactions on Mechatronics, 2018.

TEXT:
BREED HKU
World's Fastest Robotic Fish
Team Supervisor: Dr. Zhang Fu, Department of Mechanical Engineering
Executive Committee: Muhammad Saad Shahid Anwel (President), Taha Abid, Le Chi Lim, Pawan Raskoti (Tech Leads)
Guinness World Records
Introduction
The world's fastest swimming robotic fish: a robot that aims to mimic the propulsive behavior of real biological fishes, designed to swim in the complex dynamics of open waters. Our fish swims at low frequency of 4 Hz, a cruising speed of 2m/s with an input power of 150W, and can achieve high acceleration with a compact and compliant tail-like propulsion.
Design & Manufacture
The latest version consists of about 250 individual components assembled together. The dimensions are 1250mm x 150mm x 520mm with a mass of 13 kg. The parts were 3D-modelled on SolidWorks, where simulations were run to test the performance of the fish body. A scaled-down version was 3D printed or CNC machined for proof-of-concept.
The materials used to manufacture the robot are PLA plus plastic, aluminium, rubber, and acrylic. Various manufacturing methods have been used including 3D printing, CNC machining, and traditional hand tooling methods such as cutting, drilling, sanding, soldering, etc. The electrical and electronic components such as the motor, encoder, batteries, Arduino, Raspberry Pi and the wirings are sealed in acrylic tubes.
Several versions of the robotic fish were built. Each body differed in size and aerodynamic properties, with tails varying in shape, size, and material to try to achieve the best performance.
Key Technical Features
• Fully stable, buoyant, and waterproof
• All degrees of motion: roll, pitch, yaw
• Compact design with modular structure
• Energy efficient
• Maneuverability at high speeds
• Arduino Uno & Raspberry Pi 4 with pi-camera v2 module
• Wireless remote control
• Fins with servo control
Remote Control Implementation
The controls are implemented through the Raspberry Pi and Arduino, where the Arduino is used mainly for GPIO to send data to the Pi.
A custom-built controller was designed using an Arduino 220 432MHz RF receiver & transmitters (available with the Arduino).
A custom communication mechanism sends power signals and turning signals to the fish. An auto timer is also implemented to prevent the controller from overflowing the buffer of the receiver.
The orientation of the fish and fins is controlled through input from motion and orientation data, which is achieved with an inertial measurement unit (IMU).
The Pi utilizes its fast CPU to process the data, controlling servos with input from the camera while running machine learning (ML) models.
With the Sens HAT board, the Pi provides an accelerometer and gyro which maintain the orientation of the fish by a negative feedback loop and servo (fins) control.
Upcoming soon, we plan to perform system integration to connect the control systems and sensors of the robot with computer vision components.
We also aim to move towards deep reinforcement learning (Deep RL) for obstacle navigation.
Fig 1. The robotic fish - latest design.
Fig 2. A successful body and tail design.
Fig 3. Robotic fish tail.
Fig 4. Top view of the newly added fins.
Factors Affecting Performance
The relation between body length and fish swimming speed:
For a motor with given power and the same tail design, an increase in length of the fish was found to cause a decrease in swimming speed. This is because as length increased, the buoyancy, mass and inertia increased as well. Hence, newer versions of the fish were built with a longer body to improve speed.
The influence of tail design and amplitude on fish swimming speed:
It was found that with a solid tail cannot make the best of the motor. With the motor working against the rigid tail, speed was reduced. To solve this, a flexible 3D-printed tail was built. The new tail can bend and can absorb energy, significantly reducing the load on the motor. The size of the tail was also increased, as a bigger tail area allows it to push more water.
However, if a size is too large will increase the load on the motor and may even burn it. Similarly, if the amplitude of tail movement is too low, speed is low, but if amplitude is too high, it increases load. After testing several different tails and amplitudes, an optimal design was finally achieved.
Use Cases
Surveillance and Data Gathering:
Unregulated fishing practices have reduced fishery resources in local waters. As a surveillance device intended for data collection and marine research, our fish can be used to monitor illegal fishing.
Top-notch surveillance using computer vision technology can be used to look for illegal fishers and detect entangled fish in broken fishing nets.
Plastic Collection:
We aim to use this technology to tackle marine litter and water pollution, a serious issue with huge environmental impact. Computer vision can be geared towards the detection of plastics, with a garbage collector added to the fish to gather litter.
Oil Spills:
Oil spills may take weeks or years to clean up. Using a swarm of "oil sharks", this could be possible in just a few days, minimizing severe environmental effects. The technologies of UV fluorescence analyzer or non-dispersive fixed filter IR analyzer can be adapted to the fish for oil detection in water.
Aquaculture:
To improve fishing and aquaculture processes, the robotic fish can use its speed and vision technology to survey the bottom of trawling nets.
The fish can also serve as an ultrasonic bot to assist in the clean-up of biofouling (harmful buildup on fish nets).

Did you know there was an ancient pottery-making industry in HK? Do you want to uncover the secrets of how families joined together to use local resources to make ceramics? Join us on an archaeological field trip to follow the clues of past human activity through the Tai Po River valley. Learn about the historic Wun Yiu temple, trek through banana fields and jungle to discover hidden artifacts of the past, see how animals were used to grind materials, explore deep into a cave rich in porcelain minerals... Learn what archaeologists do and see if you can contribute to studying the objects of the past. Archaeology is a field that has a low level of automation but needs more. Innovation Academy
Faculty of Engineering, HKU
ONLINE WORKSHOP
AI in Law
Bridging the legal knowledge gap:
Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
3:30-4:30pm on February 23, 2022 (Wed)
In this workshop, Professor Benjamin Kao, Professor of Department of Computer Science and Co-Director of HKU Law and Technology Centre, will talk about HKU's efforts in bringing legal knowledge to the public by using Artificial Intelligence. In particular, he will give examples of how machine learning and natural language processing techniques help to make legal knowledge more accessible. These examples include using machines to understand and summarize court judgements, predict sentencing decisions, analyze the basis for judgement and provide advice.
SPEAKER
Professor Benjamin Kao
Department of Computer Science, HKU
Professor Ben Kao received his B.Sc. degree in computer studies from HKU and his PhD in computer science from Princeton University. He was a research fellow at Stanford University for 3 years before joining HKU CS in 1995. He is a co-director of HKU Law and Technology Centre, Professor Kao's research interests include data engineering and data mining.

TEXT:
Impact of Different Factors on Hyporheic Exchange in a Meandering Pool-riffle Stream
Tsz Kwan CHEUNG and Peng HUANG
Department of Civil Engineering, The University of Hong Kong

I. Introduction
Hyporheic Exchanges (HE) is the region of saturated sediment surrounding a stream which connects surface water and groundwater flow.
The overlying water with dissolved matter infiltrates into the HZ, stays there for some time, interacts with groundwater and eventually out of the HZ, resulting in hyporheic exchange (HE). This process supports physicochemical and biological reactions that are essential to river ecosystem functions.

River Restoration
Most of the rivers are designed with narrow bottom section and large upper sections of coarse streambed (Fig 2(a)). However, this design has led all ecosystems in bad river eco-system. HE transports suspended and dissolved solutes such as nutrients, contaminants, organic carbon, and oxygen into the HZ. This creates a rich mixture composed of aquatic organisms and permanent dwell there.
In recent decades, more and more stream restoration projects involve the recovery of hyporheic zone to increase its function in river ecosystem. Therefore, this study aims to examine the effectiveness of different key factors (e.g., stream discharge, slope, sinuosity and groundwater flow) on restoring HZ in a meandering channel with floodplain using flume experiments and numerical simulations.

II. Methodology
The flume model was built in a recirculating box to simulate different hydrological conditions (e.g., streamflow, slope and sinuosity). Tracer experiments were performed and results were used to quantify the impacts of baffles designs on the HE fluxes.

TEXT:
Lost Slime: A New Home
COMP3329
computer programming and game design
Our music game sets out to improve everyone's burst typing speed and stability.
Developed with Node.js, Express.js and Socket.IO, Lost Slime is a Multiplayer/Educational/Rhythm game that runs on your web browser. Written in javascript, it is designed to be lightweight and responsive to run on any machines.
Find Slimies new houses! Players in a game room compete to stack the tallest pillar to gain a high ground - which helps Slimies in spotting new locations to house. To stack a pillar block, players time their space-bars along with the music beats. But that's not it! There are phrases or sentences intertwined with, that players have to input correctly before pressing space-bar! By achieving the two objectives, Slimies can then jump on the newly stacked pillar block!

Reinforcement Learning
Methodology
Reinforcement Learning aims to find a policy for an agent to maximise its reward in its environment. We applied the Sarsa(lambda) algorithm to micromanagement in SC2. It is a model-free, off-policy reinforcement learning algorithm that uses eligibility traces for assigning temporal credit

The agent successfully learnt optimal strategies for all scenarios tested

TEXT:
Self-healing, microencapsulation and granular materials
Department of Civil Engineering, University of Hong Kong
Name: Chow Cheuk Hei Scott
Supervisor : Dr. Sérgio D.N. Lourenço
INTRODUCTION
• Foundation quality is of paramount importance to all civil engineering works. Since it governs the safety of the structures and buildings stood above it. However, settlement in foundation is found very common, in which it comes as a natural deterioration process. Maintenance work for foundation can be challenging and costly. Having said that, inspired by the adopting of self-healing capsules in concrete improvement, this study aims to mimic and incorporate similar self-healing technology in strengthening of soil.
COMPLEX COACERVATION
• a process in which two oppositely charged wall materials react to form the capsule of the core material. Gelatin and Gum Arabic are commonly used as the capsule materials. Gelatin is a protein, while Gum Arabic is a polysaccharide.
Core dispersed in aqueous solution of anionic polymer
Addition of cationic polymer solution
Interaction between polymers
Hardening/Cross linking
Drying
Coacervates with core in the center
• The main goal of this study is to examine whether self-healing materials can be encapsulated and added to the soil to improve its strength. Other objectives include the effect of pH and temperature on capsules formation through complex coacervation and the self-healing effects of microcapsules under different load application and healing time. Complex Coacervation is proposed as the method to produce microcapsules, while shear box test will be the core methodology used in assessing the self-healing ability of microcapsules when added into soil for improvement. It is hoped this study could promote the use of self-healing microcapsules as a mean for soil improvement in the engineering industry, thereby reducing the cost for maintenance of foundation and also improving the durability and safety of the structures.
SELF HEALING MECHANISM
• Capsule based self-healing, as its name suggest, the capsule is made to provide mechanical protection to the healing agent. When cracks occur, the shell of the capsule will be ruptured. As a result, the core materials inside the capsule will leak out and then undergo some chemical reactions and produce substances, which acts as glue to seal the crack together, achieving the self-healing behaviour.
(a) Before breaking capsules.
(b) After breaking capsules
The preliminary results show that capsules can be produced through complex coacervation and it has displayed some signs of self-healing effects exerted on the sand sample. Further testing will be conducted to justify the self-healing ability of the microcapsules. In the future, one will investigate the self-healing effects of the capsules under different parameters such as applied load, microcapsule content as well as healing time.

Research Highlight
Physical understanding of abnormal embryo development
Principle Investigator: Professor Yuan LIN, Associate Professor, Department of Mechanical Engineering
Introduction
Abnormal embryonic development leads to severe birth defects and diseases such as dysmelia. Recent studies have shown that the embryo of Caenorhabditis elegans (C.elegans), a model organism, undergoes abnormal elongation when cellular anisotropy and plasticity cannot be developed and maintained properly. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
Novelty of the project
To understand the physical origin of abnormal embryo elongation, we developed a dynamic model (within the framework of continuum mechanics and thermodynamics) to:
(1) elucidate how cellular anisotropy and plasticity are gradually developed in the embryo wall during its elongation;
(2) show how the elongation process is sustained and stabilized by the development of anisotropy and plasticity in cells;
(3) reveal that insufficient myosin activity and excessive severing of F-actin bundles are two major causes for abnormal embryo elongation.

Benefit to the community
This study is expected to be useful for biologists, biophysicists, and biomedical engineers. Specifically,
(1) by elucidating the exact roles of intra/inter-cellular contraction, F-actin realignment and severing/re-bundling in the elongation of embryos, this work significantly advances our physical understanding of this important process;
(2) our study also indicates that abnormal embryo elongation might be rescued by restoring myosin activity and F-actin stability. This could provide new insights for the prevention and treatment of birth defects and related diseases in the future.

Keywords:

A B S T R A C T
A procedure for the seismic analysis of underground tunnels using recorded free-field earthquakes based on the 2.5D finite/infinite element approach is presented. The near and far fields of the half space are modeled by finite and infinite elements, respectively. Using the 1D wave theory, the nodal force and displacement on the near-field boundary are computed for each spectral frequency of the earthquake. Then, equivalent seismic forces are computed for the near-field boundary for the earthquake spectrum. By assuming the soil-tunnel system to be uniform along the tunnel axis, which reduces to the 2D case for infinite transmission velocity. The horizontal and vertical components of the 1999 Chi-Chi Earthquake (TCU068) are adopted as the free-field motions in the numerical analysis. The maximal stresses and distribution patterns of the tunnel section under the P- and SV-waves are thoroughly studied by the 2.5D and 2D approaches, which should prove useful to the design of underground tunnels.

TEXT:
Lost Slime: A New Home
COMP3329
computer programming and game design
Our music game sets out to improve everyone's burst typing speed and stability.
Developed with Node.js, Express.js and Socket.IO, Lost Slime is a Multiplayer/Educational/Rhythm game that runs on your web browser. Written in javascript, it is designed to be lightweight and responsive to run on any machines.
Find Slimies new houses! Players in a game room compete to stack the tallest pillar to gain a high ground - which helps Slimies in spotting new locations to house. To stack a pillar block, players time their space-bars along with the music beats. But that's not it! There are phrases or sentences intertwined with, that players have to input correctly before pressing space-bar! By achieving the two objectives, Slimies can then jump on the newly stacked pillar block!
With the theme set as improving everyone's typing proficiency with music, it could be cheerful-lighthearted, or mechanically intensive. We have designed an additional beat-mapper program to translate music pieces into custom track information used by the game, in json format. Which means players can create authentic mappings with their favorite music! We sincerely you could enjoy the game and offer us your precious like!

TEXT:
Evolving Human-Like Micromanagement in StarCraft II with Neuro-Evolution and Reinforcement Learning
Supervisor - Dr. Dirk Schneiders
Group Members - Fawad Masood Desmukh, Zain-Ul-Abidin
Deliverables
Applied Neuroevolution and Reinforcement Learning to SC2 micromanagement
Built frameworks for machine learning agents to interact with SC2
Generic training agents with helper functions to speed up development
Trained agents that successfully learnt strategies for micro-scenarios
StarCraft II Map sets
Extensive Testing
Reinforcement Learning
Methodology
Reinforcement Learning aims to find a policy for an agent to maximise its reward in its environment. We applied the Sarsa(lambda) algorithm to micromanagement in SC2. It is a model-free, off-policy reinforcement learning algorithm that uses eligibility traces for assigning temporal credit
Sarsa Agent
State – Self Unit Type, Unit Type of Closest Enemy, Distance to closest enemy, Scaled Relative Power, Is Together, Weapon Cooldown
Actions – Attack, Engage, Retreat, Scatter
Results
The Sarsa Agent was applied to various complex scenarios that required creative micromanagement strategies such as kiting/hit-and-run, effective unit positioning, attack timing and evaluating the strengths and weaknesses of yourself versus the enemy. The agent successfully learnt optimal strategies for all scenarios tested
