Conclusion
Our implementations show the potential of neuroevolution and reinforcement learning for complex control problems. Through effective experimentation in StarCraft II, one can transfer the findings of this project to real-world problems such as evolving effective robotic-controllers. Our open-source NEAT-SC2 training framework along with extensive testing done with our agents represent meaningful contributions to the artificial intelligence and StarCraft II communities
NEAT Agent
Neural Network Inputs – Current Health, Weapon Cooldown, Weapon ranges (Self/Enemy), Movement Speed (Self/Enemy), Enemy in-range. Recurrent Previous Command, Distances to map edges, Enemy directional detection inputs
Neural Network Outputs – Fight/Flee, Displacement in x-axis, Displacement in y-axis
Results
The NEAT Agent successfully learnt the kiting/hit-and-run strategy for a ranged vs melee matchup in a restricted space. It learnt the optimal kiting strategy for different kind of ranged units which was robust to different starting configurations. The evolved microcontroller performed well even if the number of enemy units was increased. In addition, networks were also evolved to learn the melee-vs-ranged matchup

To deal with this unsatisfied demand, we choose to facilitate an advanced query type - Spatial Pattern Matching (SPM), which is a new type of spatial group keyword query raised in recent research. Led by our supervisor, Dr. Reynold C. K. Cheng, its solutions have been well-discussed in theory. In our project, we want to fit these theories in this real-life scenario by resolving practical issues, as well as realizing some additional functionalities related to property searching.
In the end, we have developed a standalone web-based application to demonstrate the importance and practicality of this newly proposed functionality.

Self-healing, microencapsulation and granular materials
Department of Civil Engineering, University of Hong Kong
Name: Chow Cheuk Hei Scott
Supervisor : Dr. Sérgio D.N. Lourenço
INTRODUCTION
• Foundation quality is of paramount importance to all civil engineering works. Since it governs the safety of the structures and buildings stood above it. However, settlement in foundation is found very common, in which it comes as a natural deterioration process. Maintenance work for foundation can be challenging and costly. Having said that, inspired by the adopting of self-healing capsules in concrete improvement, this study aims to mimic and incorporate similar self-healing technology in strengthening of soil.
COMPLEX COACERVATION
• a process in which two oppositely charged wall materials react to form the capsule of the core material. Gelatin and Gum Arabic are commonly used as the capsule materials. Gelatin is a protein, while Gum Arabic is a polysaccharide.
Core dispersed in aqueous solution of anionic polymer
Addition of cationic polymer solution
Interaction between polymers
Hardening/Cross linking
Drying
Coacervates with core in the center
• The main goal of this study is to examine whether self-healing materials can be encapsulated and added to the soil to improve its strength. Other objectives include the effect of pH and temperature on capsules formation through complex coacervation and the self-healing effects of microcapsules under different load application and healing time. Complex Coacervation is proposed as the method to produce microcapsules, while shear box test will be the core methodology used in assessing the self-healing ability of microcapsules when added into soil for improvement. It is hoped this study could promote the use of self-healing microcapsules as a mean for soil improvement in the engineering industry, thereby reducing the cost for maintenance of foundation and also improving the durability and safety of the structures.
SELF HEALING MECHANISM
• Capsule based self-healing, as its name suggest, the capsule is made to provide mechanical protection to the healing agent. When cracks occur, the shell of the capsule will be ruptured. As a result, the core materials inside the capsule will leak out and then undergo some chemical reactions and produce substances, which acts as glue to seal the crack together, achieving the self-healing behaviour.
(a) Before breaking capsules.
(b) After breaking capsules
The preliminary results show that capsules can be produced through complex coacervation and it has displayed some signs of self-healing effects exerted on the sand sample. Further testing will be conducted to justify the self-healing ability of the microcapsules. In the future, one will investigate the self-healing effects of the capsules under different parameters such as applied load, microcapsule content as well as healing time.

Impact of Different Factors on Hyporheic Exchange in a Meandering Pool-riffle Stream
Tsz Kwan CHEUNG and Peng HUANG
Department of Civil Engineering, The University of Hong Kong

I. Introduction
Hyporheic Exchanges (HE) is the region of saturated sediment surrounding a stream which connects surface water and groundwater flow.
The overlying water with dissolved matter infiltrates into the HZ, stays there for some time, interacts with groundwater and eventually out of the HZ, resulting in hyporheic exchange (HE). This process supports physicochemical and biological reactions that are essential to river ecosystem functions.

River Restoration
Most of the rivers are designed with narrow bottom section and large upper sections of coarse streambed (Fig 2(a)). However, this design has led all ecosystems in bad river eco-system. HE transports suspended and dissolved solutes such as nutrients, contaminants, organic carbon, and oxygen into the HZ. This creates a rich mixture composed of aquatic organisms and permanent dwell there.
In recent decades, more and more stream restoration projects involve the recovery of hyporheic zone to increase its function in river ecosystem. Therefore, this study aims to examine the effectiveness of different key factors (e.g., stream discharge, slope, sinuosity and groundwater flow) on restoring HZ in a meandering channel with floodplain using flume experiments and numerical simulations.

II. Methodology
The flume model was built in a recirculating box to simulate different hydrological conditions (e.g., streamflow, slope and sinuosity). Tracer experiments were performed and results were used to quantify the impacts of baffles designs on the HE fluxes.

HAND GESTURE
MULTIPLAYER MODE
Team Leader: Chim Tsz Sang
Team members: Man Yu Ching Ling Tsz Shuen
Supervisor: Dr.T.W. Chim
GOODBYE TO TOUCHSCREEN
Touchscreen has become a standardised technology.
Developers often limit users' hand gestures on the mobile device by touchscreen instead of allowing them to interact with virtual objects in reality.
REAL GESTURE CONTROL
Use your own hand to interact with the virtual objects.
DRAG the cube and move it around in a physical space.
DROP the cube to build a tower.
MULTIPLAYER MODE
Our Multiplayer mode links the positions of different players, sharing the same world map across their mobile devices in real time.
THE EDUCATIONAL POSSIBILITIES OF AR
AR simulations enable students to observe phenomena they would not be able to see first-hand. E.g. laboratory experiments may be too costly.
SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
1. HAND GESTURE RECOGNITION CONTROL
Gesture-based control methods provide players a more natural and realistic approach to interact with virtual game objects. In addition, players can have 3D control with their hands over the real space instead of 2D control over touchscreens. This project will not create a new hand tracking and recognition system but aims to integrate existing hand gesture recognition control systems as the main input method in a bid to create an immersive gaming experience.
2. WORLD MAP SHARING AMONG DEVICES
The key to make an immersive AR game is to integrate multiplayer functionality in AR gaming development. Multiplayer mode requires a network to link the position of each player, sharing the same world map across different mobile devices. The APIs in ARCore and ARKit have similar functions but they are platform-specific. To better advance the existing APIs, this project aims to build a multiplayer functionality that can achieve a shared world map.
In conclusion, this project focuses on three major aspects, which include a cross-platform AR developing framework, a HGR control scheme, as well as a cross-platform shared world map for multiplayers.
ABSTRACT
With the increasing popularity and computation power of mobile devices, AR (Augmented reality) is more accessible. It has a high potential for revolution human-machine interaction. Video games, especially mobile games, can utilize AR technology to provide an immersive user experience. Without using expensive high-end AR devices such as HoloLens, mobile AR experience usually lacks interactions between users and virtual objects due to limited size and control interface of the device. This project is to develop an AR interactive mobile game prototype under a cross-platform development framework and includes hand gesture control and world map sharing.
We developed an Android AR game application prototype using ARFoundation in Unity. A hand gesture control scheme is built using the Manonotion SDK. The world map sharing is achieved using Google Cloud Anchor API and the multiplayer functionality was done by using Photon Bolt.

Overview
A drug prediction system that uses knowledge graph (KG) analysis to recommend existing drugs that can be repurposed to treat COVID-19

Proposed drug candidates are ranked by integrating three scores that are generated by analysis of the KG using three established techniques: Motif analysis, PageRank analysis, and Machine Learning

Clean, easy to use interface allows medical experts and researchers to efficiently identify promising drug candidates for further investigation through clinical trials

TEXT:
HKU ROBOMASTER-AI
PROJECT FRAMEWORK
Our project operates on a ROS (Robot Operating System)-based codebase. Through collaborative development from existing open-source code, we present a competition-level solution to our robotics. The codebase involves atomic operations on robot detection, decision, motion planning, etc. We've open-sourced our code in HKU-Robomaster.
DETECTION
To target the armor of the enemy robots, we deployed an industrial camera and an Nvidia-TX2 AI development board in the car. Considering that the aiming task is sensitive to position information and detection speed, we avoided the traditional use of CNN and used DETR as our automatic aiming baseline. Further development will involve quantifying the model and coupling the detection module as well as the muzzle control module to improve further aiming speed and accuracy.
Figure 2: The output of the detection module.
LOCALIZATION
To improve the robustness of positioning, we use multimodal information (robot-mounted lidar, depth camera, optical camera), which give possible estimates of the current position through their respective data processing programs and simply combine them using the Kalman filter algorithm in the decision making. Further consideration will be given to the collaborative processing of these data.
Figure 3: The multimodal information used by localization
ALGORITHM
We prepared two plans for decision making, one works on the behavior tree, and another is based on Deep Reinforcement Learning. We choose the behavior tree as a demo since the training result is not yet satisfactory.
We also use the heap-optimized A* algorithm to plan the robot's path. To ensure that the car can reach the destination quickly and safely, we mark the dangerous area on the map as high-cost. And we shrink the empty part of the node to speed up the code.
Figure 4: The possible route planned by our A* algorithm
WHAT ARE WE GOING TO DO?
We believe there is something more precious than the prizes of the competition. We are committed to training the team's collaborative development ability and hardware and software coordination ability through RMUA. We want to stimulate students' interest in research and programming and form a community to share their ideas.

TEXT:
Trigger-specific Self-prevention and Preliminary Diagnosis of Depression using Flash Stimulus and GSR sensor
Presenter: Qi Baigian Tong Anze Supervisor: Dr. W.N. Lee (Ph.D., M.Phil., M.S., B.S.), Associate Professor
Introduction
Depression is a common neurological disorder, from which 7.2% of people are estimated to suffer[1]. Meanwhile, different studies show that undiagnosed depression comprises a large share of all the cases, ranging from 40% to 75%[2]. This disease is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and the economic cost from an untreated patient can be up to $9300 USD[2, 3]. As the current pandemic puts people at a higher risk of getting depression, a better prevention and diagnosis solution is needed to avoid severer people and economic loss[4,5]—the current technologies for prevention and diagnosis such as Questionnaires, Internet Behavioral Guidance, and Biomarkers Imaging, however, lack trigger-specific property. Meanwhile, finding the trigger and solving the problem or offering trigger-based psychotherapy is essential for treatment[6]. On the other hand, most of those technologies are clinical-based and are not available to ordinary people to raise their self-awareness of their mental health. The cost and stigmatization towards the psychologist have impeded people from approaching the professionals to prevent their symptoms from deterioration[7]. This study will discuss a breakthrough idea using flash-stimulus to find triggers and provide a possible solution to ordinary people for trigger-specific self-prevention and preliminary diagnosis using a GSR sensor.
Current Shortcoming
Prevention
Distinguish Normal, Stress, and Depression
Not trigger specific
Clinical based—expensive
Complex and accuracy
Poorly prepared towards psychotherapy
Diagnosis
Data-based
Easy to use
Self-operating diagnosis
GSR sensor
GSR sensor's measurement can reflect the subject's emotional change. The measurand is skin's resistance, which can be affected by the emotional change through the pathway, as illustrated in Figure 1.
Emotional Change → Affect → Sweat Gland → Secretion → Move or not → Change → Skin Resistance
Conclusion
Globally, depression is a prevalent neurological disorder and can cause severe economic loss. Besides the direct burden on the health care system, the indirect cost on the undiagnosed patients are substantial[2]. Currently, the prevention and diagnosis technologies lack a way to raise self-awareness and provide trigger-specific solutions [5]. This lacking impedes people from preventing the depression deterioration of deterioration at an early stage, thus causing more severe people and economic loss. To break down their limitations, we propose a plan to give ordinary people a way to make trigger-specific self-prevention and preliminary diagnoses. Using the GSR sensor and the strategy of flash-stimulus, we provide a low-cost but user-friendly plan to help the users know better about their mental status. Similar experiments showing that using flash-stimulus to find depression triggers is promising.
In the future, depression's prevalence is likely to grow[15]. WHO has estimated that by the year 2030, unipolar major depression will become the leading cause of disease burden[17]. So, the research in this part corresponds to the future need and is expected to promote people's livelihood.

STAR lab.
HINCare: An Intelligent Timebanking System for Elderly Care
Team Member: Hu Zhenwei
Supervisor: Prof. Reynold Cheng
In Hong Kong, the number of elderly citizens is estimated to rise to 1/3 of the population (2.27 million) in year 2037.
As they age and become more frail, the demand for support services (e.g., providing domestic or escort services) will increase significantly in the coming years.
However, there is a severe lack of manpower to meet this demand due to the aging workforce and shortage of employees. There is thus a strong need of voluntary or part-time helpers for taking care of elders.
This is why we introduce HINCare, an app that encourages mutual-help in the community.
HINCare adopts the concept of timebanking, where each user has his/her own account to store the amount of time ("time credits").
Users can exchange their "time credits" with other users for providing services or receiving other services. Moreover, HINCare uses HIN (Heterogeneous Information Network) to recommend helpers to elders.
HIN is a huge graph which stores the relationship information among elders, helpers and NGOs.
We use HIN to model the recommendation process of matching elders and helpers. Our team uses HIN and AI technologies for matching elders and helpers. It is based on our recent research results.
HINCare is a cloud-based system. Administrators of elderly care centers use the system through a convenient web-based interface to perform daily tasks (e.g., task assignment, event announcement, and user profile management). The system is easy to learn and use. The system is generic and flexible, allowing NGOs to join our scheme easily.
AI Recommendation of Volunteers
Use of HIN Algorithm to recommend suitable volunteers to the service requesters
Real-time Web Portal Monitoring
Together with the mobile App, NGO's staff can monitor and follow up with the volunteering Services Progress, enhancing work efficiency
Time Credit Account Review
We advertise our HINCare mobile app to benefit more elderly and encourage them to join NGOs so that they can easily find helpers on HINCare platform. We also encourage elders to provide services and intend for new activities on our platform in exchange of time credits, which they can consume them later for receiving help from services.
We organize tutorial sessions and cooperate with different NGOs to teach the elderly how to use our HINCare mobile app.
We adopt HIN (Heterogeneous Information Network) in our project to facilitate the recommendation process. We then utilize fine-tuned Transl (Translating Embeddings for Modeling Multi-relational Data). We also use other models such as BPR, Top-pop, Transi to perform the actual recommendations. HR (Hit Ratio) and NDCG (Discounted Cumulative Gain) are used as the metrics for measuring model effectiveness.

TEXT:
Eco.ly
iGEM HKU 2021
A plastic degradation project
The Problem
Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is one of the most commonly used plastics worldwide. Cheap to produce, durable, and flexible; these properties make plastics ubiquitous and versatile in their use. Today, they are found in products ranging from food storage to textile to medical devices. However, the same properties that make plastics attractive also make it difficult to break down.
79%
of PET ends up in landfills or is thrown away (PlasticsEurope, 2019)
450
years in order for PET to fully break down (Armstrong, 2021)
Current Solutions
Current methods of dealing with PET waste include dumping into landfills, incineration, and mechanical and chemical recycling. However, these efforts are not fully sustainable.
Landfills require a lot of space; incineration release toxic gases such as methane in the process, and different types of PET make chemically breaking down PET expensive. The newest recycling plant in Hong Kong, New Life Plastics, plans only to recycle specific types of PET.
Decreasing plastic waste is a priority not because we are running out of landfill space, but also because it impacts human health. Impurities from plastic can leach into the water they interact with different organisms. Birds and fish can ingest or become tangled in plastic, where they suffocate, starve, or drown. 38% of 555 fish species surveyed by Savoca (2021) had ingested plastic. This means there is a high chance that we are also indirectly consuming plastics and the toxins they release. COVID-19 is only exacerbating the plastics waste issue as more eateries are using single-use takeout containers and utensils and using single-use plastic gloves.
Our Solution: Eco.ly
We create Eco.ly, a self-sustaining co-culture of the bacterium E. coli and cyanobacterium S. elongatus that can degrade PET. Genetically engineered S. elongatus is engineered to secrete enzymes for their photosynthesis. This system is taken by E. coli - also genetically engineered using it as an energy source to produce the enzyme PETase and MHTase.
The TPA and EG monomers can then be used to resynthesise new PHA bioplastics using the genus Pseudomonas. Our system involves the design of three plasmids: the PETase and MHTase producing plasmid, the sucrose uptake plasmid for E. coli, and a sucrose secretion plasmid for S. elongatus.
E. coli PET degrading
plasmid
TPA, EG
S. elongatus sucrose
secretion plasmid
Future Plans & Next Steps
Much of our system remains to be experimentally verified in the future. In the future, we plan on placing our system in our hardware to verify that the biological components will work as expected. We also hope to be able more accurately quantify our system's PET degradation rates to identify areas of improvement.

TEXT:
The University of Hong Kong
INFLUENCE OF DISINFECTANTS ON
MICROBIAL WATER TREATMENT PROCESSES
By Chan Tszyu, BEng (CivE)
Supervisor: Dr. G.Y.A. Tan
During the COVID-19 pandemic, the use of disinfectants has surged in order to contain the spread of the virus. Many disinfectants will be sent to wastewater treatment plants after use for treatment before discharging back to the environment. Nevertheless, studies have shown that large amount of disinfectants can inhibit biological reactions during the wastewater treatment process. The activated sludge process is particularly susceptible to disinfectants. Hence, this study aims to investigate the inhibitory effects of two common active ingredients of disinfectants, namely QACs and sodium hypochlorite, on the activated sludge process.
Quaternary Ammonium Compounds (QACs)
In general, QACs are considered as biodegradable in the activated sludge process since microorganisms in activated sludge utilize QACs as food and energy sources. Yet, studies have shown that high concentration of QACs can inhibit respiratory enzymes in activated sludge, causing activated sludge process to be interfered. Therefore, it is important to measure the percentage inhibition for each concentration of QACs to the activated sludge system.
Sodium Hypochlorite
Since sodium hypochlorite contains chlorine, it is sometimes added to activated sludge for chlorination and to control filamentous bulking problem. However, chlorination is not selective because it also affects COD removal rates and nitrification processes. Excessive sodium hypochlorite can affect the activities of activated sludge flocs. Therefore, it is necessary to define the concentration of sodium hypochlorite that leads to inhibition of the activated sludge process.
Schematic diagram showing how QACs inhibit respiratory enzymes in activated sludge
METHODLOGY
Collect activated sludge samples from Sha Tin Sewage Treatment Works. To ensure that the samples have sufficient solids concentration, synthetic wastewater will be added to the samples before the experiment.
Various doses of QACs and sodium hypochlorite will be added to the samples separately.
After six hours of retention time, the concentration of COD, NH4+, NO3- and NO2- will be measured to examine the percentage inhibition of the two disinfectants on the COD rates and nitrification processes.
SIGNIFICANCE OF THE STUDY
To raise public awareness of the ancillary environmental impacts of disinfectants
To help the public in selecting disinfectants that have high efficacy while minimizing environmental impacts

Objective: To obtain 3D-printable UHPC by determining its fresh state and hardened state properties.

Printing UHPC
Before printing UHPC, we need to design the concrete mix for UHPC. The performance of UHPC varies with different concrete components and mixing proportion.

After mixing the concrete, it is time to test whether the UHPC mix is printable and whether it possess ultra-high performance. Since no 3D concrete printing machine is available to us, we have to make one ourselves!
Robot Arm

3D Printing System

Methodology
Sample Preparation
Mix the adequate ratios of raw materials with water. It is used for Slump & Slump-flow Test and Pumping & Printing test. The sample is also used for casting cement cubes for the compressive tests.
Slump & Slump-flow Test
The slump height and slump-flow diameter are determined to find out the workability of the specimens.
Compressive Test
The compressive strength of concrete can be determined by compressing a concrete cube using the ELE Machine.
Pumping & Printing Test
The continuity and the existence of void are checked by using a mortar pump, then larger structures can be printed using our 3D Printing System.

Conclusion
Up to now, several mix designs were made and tested. We have successfully printed some UHPC models, and their strength reached 120 MPa, which is much higher than conventional vibrating concrete of 30-60 MPa. By designing UHPC that can be smoothly pumped and 3D-printed, we hope to promote this new way of construction method to the construction industry!

Line-follower sensor is used to guide the robot following a pre-defined pathway. As black object could absorb infrared light, by placing two infrared light LEDs and infrared receivers side by side, we could use them to detect whether the robot is following the "black" path.
Jansen's linkage is a planar leg mechanism designed by the kinetic sculptor Theo Jansen to generate a smooth walking motion. Jansen has used his mechanism in a variety of kinetic sculptures which are known as Strandbeesten (Dutch for "beach beasts"). Jansen's linkage bears artistic as well as mechanical merit for its simulation of organic walking motion using a simple rotary input. These leg mechanisms have applications in mobile robotics and in gait analysis.

Faculty of Engineering
THE UNIVERSITY OF HONG KONG
PERfECT Viral Sewage Monitoring System
NAFISA HUMAYRA | LAI CHUN KIT | ZHAO YAZHOU | RACHEL NATALIE | LIN AIJING
Background
Learning from Covid, we have realized how critical it was to detect the origin of a virus outbreak. From tracking clusters, we are able to have preventive measures implemented as soon as possible, which undeniably reduces the impact of an outbreak in all aspects. Sewage monitoring has been under the spotlight for being an accurate indicator of a possible spread and hence our team has curated a sensor that effectively detects viruses for monitoring.
The Importance of Sewage Monitoring
EARLY DETECTION | OPTIMAL SAMPLE | DATA COLLECTION
Current Challenges
1. Labour intensive: manual sample collection, PCR, and reporting
2. Long Duration: 5.5 hours
3. Not Scalable: one RT-qPCR process for sample to detect one virus
Objective
Make a real-time, scalable, cheaper, and digital sewage monitoring system to reduce cost, labour, and duration
PERfECT's High Sensitivity
ElectroChemical Electrode + Transistor → 100 X More Sensitive
How the PERFECT system works?
From viral shedding of an infected person, parts of the virus, such as the nucleocapsid protein, are present in the sewage sample. As the DNA aptamers on the electrochemical transistor catch these target proteins, PERFECT will transmit data through BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy), to a network coordination point, which will transmit the data wirelessly to the cloud. Authorities can be notified in around 10 minutes from when the virus is detected. Thus, authorities can quickly implement the measures needed and decrease the likelihood of an uncontrolled outbreak.
PERfECT vs RT-qPCR
Comparison of RT-qPCR and PERFECT Sewage Monitoring System
| PCR | Our system |
| --- | --- |
| 97% time saved | 5.5 hours |
| 0.17% cost | 10 min |
| Reusable? | 5,799 USD |
| Yes! | 10 USD |
| Yes! | Customizability of the PERFECT Sewage Monitoring System |
| SARS-CoV-2 | Zika |
| HIV/AIDS | Ebola |
| Hepatitis | Measles |
Influenza
Future Uses
1. By the long-term monitoring of virus levels in sewage, governments can determine whether infections are rising or falling in an area and develop up-to-date health policies to limit the spread of disease.
2. Identify clusters of future outbreaks or epidemics to curb the spread.

The Impact of ChatGPT on Problem-Based Learning in Medical Education: A Comparative Study on an Anaphylaxis Tutorial
Sheung Chit Ng, Wing San Yiu, Derrick H M Chan, Yee Man Au-Yeung, Zak Song, Hoi Chak Ng,
Ching Hei So
Philip Hei Li, Shilpa Basavaraj Purdal, Kendrick Co Shih
Li Ka Shing Faculty of Medicine, The University of Hong Kong
HKU Med
BACKGROUND
• Generative AI particularly ChatGPT provides many promises in healthcare (1-3), with important implications for medical education (4)
• Despite its promise, the role of generative AI in medical education remains unclear and controversial (5,6)
AIMS
To evaluate how the use of ChatGPT in problem-based learning (PBL) affects medical students' ability to achieve learning outcomes (LO), and other education outcomes using a pilot randomised controlled trial.
To evaluate students' perception of the role of ChatGPT in medical education.
To evaluate the performance of ChatGPT GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4.0 models in solving the PBL case.
METHODS
Part I: Randomised controlled trial
Junior MBBS students (n=9)
Control group (n=4)
Intervention group (Uses ChatGPT) (n=5)
Randomisation
ChatGPT
(1) Performance marked by tutor A (randomly assigned)
(2) Evaluation form
Responses marked by the case writer (with blinding)
Part II: GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4.0
PBL case fed into ChatGPT
Using GPT-3.5 to solve the PBL case
Using GPT-4.0 to solve the PBL case
Results & Discussion
(a) Student learning outcomes (LO)
(b) Student Performance
(c) Students' perceived that the PBL tutorial helped
(d) Students' perceived that ChatGPT helped with / will help with the following:
(e) Students' perceived that ChatGPT helped with / will help with the following:
(f) ChatGPT learning outcomes (LO)
Overall: 67% of students agreed that ChatGPT should be incorporated in this PBL tutorial
CONCLUSIONS
ChatGPT helped students achieve the learning outcomes in this PBL tutorial, and could help students obtain factual knowledge and provide clinically relevant suggestions.
While most students agreed that ChatGPT should be incorporated in this PBL tutorial, there are concerns about the risk of automation bias which could hinder the development of clinical reasoning skills.
Both GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.0 models of ChatGPT could achieve the PBL learning outcomes with minimal prompting.
While the adoption of generative AI in medical education brings promise, this should be done carefully while considering the skillsets required for future clinicians in the AI era.

Quadruped robots offer several advantages for multi-terrain traversal due to their high stability, ability to negotiate uneven surfaces, and potential for redundancy in leg movements. Multi-terrain hexapods have diverse applications. They can be used in search and rescue operations, exploration of challenging environments, surveillance tasks, agricultural applications, and even entertainment or educational purposes.
Modular Robot structure
Extended legs are beneficial for climbing stairs, and a square-shaped plate enhances balance during walking. Multiple-layered structures facilitate inserting different sensors on the robot.
Inverse Kinematics algorithm for bio-inspired gait
Quadruped Inverse Kinematics (IK) is essential for enabling four-legged robots to move realistically and efficiently. These algorithms determine the joint configurations needed to position the robot's feet accurately, maintaining dynamic stability across various terrains. By mimicking natural animal gaits, IK improves the robot's ability to navigate obstacles and interact effectively with its environment.
Capability of stair climbing
The Spider Robot, inspired by spider biomechanics, adeptly navigates stairs using articulated legs for enhanced stability and flexibility. Equipped with advanced motion control algorithms, it could potentially handle complex terrains, making it ideal for search and rescue, industrial maintenance, and surveillance in inaccessible areas.

140. The art of those far-off days provided a gentler purpose for iron.

TEXT:
The Rainbow Passage

When the sunlight strikes raindrops in the air, they act as a prism and form a rainbow.
The rainbow is a division of white light into many beautiful colors. These take the shape of a long round arch, with its path high above, and its two ends apparently beyond the horizon. There is , according to legend, a boiling pot of gold at one end.
People look, but no one ever finds it. When a man looks for something beyond his reach, his friends say he is looking for the pot of gold at the end of the rainbow.
Throughout the centuries people have explained the rainbow in various ways. Some have accepted it as a miracle without physical explanation. To the Hebrews it was a token that there would be no more universal floods. The Greeks used to imagine that it was a sign from the gods to foretell war or heavy rain. The Norsemen considered the rainbow as a bridge over which the gods passed from earth to their home in the sky.
Others have tried to explain the phenomenon physically. Aristotle thought that the rainbow was caused by reflection of the sun's rays by the rain. Since then physicists have found that it is not reflection, but refraction by the raindrops which causes the rainbows. Many complicated ideas about the rainbow have been formed.
The difference in the rainbow depends considerably upon the size of the drops, and the width of the colored band increases as the size of the drops increases. The actual primary rainbow observed is said to be the effect of super-imposition of a number of bows. If the red of the second bow falls upon the green of the first, the result is to give a bow with an abnormally wide yellow band, since red and green light when mixed form yellow. This is a very common type of bow, one showing mainly red and yellow, with little or no green or blue.

From Fairbanks, G. (1960). Voice and articulation drillbook, 2nd edn. New York: Harper & Row. pp124-139.

In this workshop, you will learn about the basics of using Unity Engine and how to build a VR game using the official Unity package XR-interaction toolKit. The XR interaction Toolkit package is a high-level, component-based, interaction system for creating VR and AR experiences. Games built can be deployed in various VR/AR devices such as HTC VIVE, HoloLens, Oculus, etc. The workshop will serve as a brief introduction to how you can setup an Oculus VR Headset, develop a simple VR game on Unity via XR-interaction toolkit and deploy it onto the Oculus device. Prior knowledge on Unity and basic coding concepts would be great but not essential.

The model is divided into three categories:

De-reverb and de-delay models (by FoxJoy):
(1) MDX-Net: The best choice for stereo reverb removal but cannot remove mono reverb;
(234) DeEcho: Removes delay effects. Aggressive mode removes more thoroughly than Normal mode. DeReverb additionally removes reverb and can remove mono reverb, but not very effectively for heavily reverberated high-frequency content.
De-reverb/de-delay notes:
1. The processing time for the DeEcho-DeReverb model is approximately twice as long as the other two DeEcho models.
2. The MDX-Net-DeReverb model is quite slow.
3. The recommended cleanest configuration is to apply MDX-Net first and then DeEcho-Aggressive.

Club Grenade is a fast-paced multiplayer action game which a group of friends and family of all ages, at a maximum of four players, can enjoy. In the game each player controls a character who inflicts damage on high-tech facility by fights with col shading and outline.

TEXT:
UTM DIC
THE UNIVERSITY OF HONG KONG
DEPARTMENT OF MECHANICAL ENGINEERING
CAPSTONE PROJECT GROUP D04
PROJECT TOPIC
Development of Universal Testing Machine with Digital Image Correlation System for Soft/Biomaterials
OUR OBJECTIVES
The capstone project team will develop a universal testing machine specifically for soft and biomaterials with the minimal scale and production cost, such that in order to increase the availability of the universal testing machine, and enhancing the development and research on the new biomaterials. In addition to the development of UTM, the team will also investigate and provide an overview on the possibility of integrating the contactless optical measurement technique.
TESTING PROCEDURES
How to use the Universal Testing Machine to perform tensile testing together with Digital Image Correlation Analysis
1. Sample preparation (Applying black speckle patterns on testing sample by using airbrush)
2. Fixing the sample on the grip
3. Applying load to the sample and Capturing the images during elongation
4. Processing images
5. DIC Analysis and Post-DIC Analysis
6. Computation of Stress-Strain Curve

TEXT:
BazaAR - Augmented reality in Retail
typ18064
Anchit Sam
Archishma Verma
Dr. HF Ting
The Problem
The retail market in Hong Kong is dominated by three main types.
Physical stores, Online Stores and Hawkers.
Owing to Hong Kong's high rentals, retailers find it very expensive to set up physical stores.
Hawking industry on the other hand provides livelihood to more than 13000 people, but is likely to die soon due to government rules and regulations.
71% customers would shop at retailer more if they offered augmented reality as it would give them a chance to make sound shopping decisions
Our Solution
An all new intuitive shopping experience where hawkers can create 3D models of their products just by clicking photographs and display them in Augmented Reality for potential buyers to see and interact with.
B
BAZAAR
Bringing shops closer to you
A retail application that uses Augmented Reality and Photogrammetry
Features
Create detailed 3D models
Interaction in Augmented Reality
Friendly User Interface
The application provides an interface for shopkeepers to upload several pictures of there product, which would be modelled using photogrammetry to create detailed 3D models.
The 3D models would be spawned using AR for the user to place in his/her room setting. They would be able to visualise it accurately so as to make a sound purchasing decision
The UI serves as a platform between shopkeepers and customers which is as easy to use as any other e-commerce application
Technical Pipeline
model creation
Shopkeeper uploads images of product with their own camera using BSImage Picker ->
Rest calls to ReCAP API using Alamofire ->
Server sends a 3D model in the form of a URL -> URL added to the backend database ->
object spawning
Customer browses through various products on the application ->
When he/she selects a product, a 3D model is pulled from the database ->
3D model is spawned using ARKit ->
User Interacts with the 3D model by scaling and rotating ->
User makes a sound purchasing decision

SMART OZONE STERILIZING ROBOT
Ozone is the most efficient disinfectant against all types of microorganisms.
It is effective in eliminating virus, fungi and bacteria.
All the structures macromolecular cells are altered, decomposed and disappeared due to its high capacity for direct oxidation.
CLOUD
Our cloud platform is built by ASPNet and is made for two purposes. First: for ozone concentration tracking. Air quality inside the sterilization room can be monitored to ensure that it is safe enough for humans to get in. Second: for robot location tracking, we can have real-time tracking of a robot during product delivery to avoid off-tracking and losing.
ROS
Robot Operating System-ROS. ROS is more like a framework responsible for communicating and operating the various components of the robot. Take the walking of the robot as an example. To make the robot walk, it needs to control the motor underneath, and there are some obstacle avoidance sensors. The functions in ROS act like a bridge for the controlling programs of both motors and the sensors to communicate and coordinate.
AGV
Agv means automated guided vehicle which can follow the wires on the floor. Our purchased agv can be controlled by ROS language and it has vision camera for navigation. We would set the route for the agv to fit the layout of the elderly home. To avoid the collision between the agv and the elderslies, our agv will design with highly maneuverable with suitable size and moving speed.

TEXT:
Multifunctional Filters for Protecting Public Health
Professor Chuyang TANG
Professor Department of Civil Engineering
Clean water and clean air are vital for public health.
This project focuses on developing high-efficiency and environmentally sustainable filters for removing harmful air/water pollutants.
The team has developed novel architectures and functionalities for the filters to achieve high permeance, high removal efficiency, and excellent reusability.
Novelty of the project
The developed highly porous, multifunctional, and nanostructured filters can be used in various applications such as water filtration, air filtration, and air purification. The major innovation features of the project include: 1) highly efficient air filtration (e.g., >99% removal of 0.3 µm particles, indicating excellent efficiency for removing fine particulate matter, bacteria, and viruses); 2) rapid water filters that are electricity-free, chemical-free, compact, and portable; 3) reusable filter designs for improved sustainability.
Benefits to the community
The project will create great benefits to the communities which include:
1. Meeting urgent public demand for clean air amid COVID-19. Our air filters offer long-lasting, high-efficiency, and sustainable air filtration to address the critical challenges on air quality during COVID-19.
2. Providing clean drinking water for people with urgent needs. Our water filter technology enables rapid purification of contaminated water sources without electricity or chemical addition, and high-efficiency removal without the need of electricity and chemical addition.
3. Improving public health by reducing exposure to harmful pollutants in both air and water. The reusable nature of our air filters extend their lifespan and effectively reduce the generation of waste from exhausted filters.
Achievement of the project
This project has got 6 awards, including HKU Innovator Award, MIT Technology Review's Innovators Under 35, etc.
It also generated 9 papers and 1 patent.
The team successfully licensed the water filter technology to a company and collaborated with potential filter manufacturers on several contract research projects.

TEXT:
Unravelling How SARS-CoV-2 Has Been Transmitted
Professor Yuguo Li
Chair Professor Department of Mechanical Engineering
How is the emerging new SARS-CoV-2 transmitted? This has been one of the major challenges for effective intervention since the COVID-19 pandemic emerged in late 2019.
Following our continuous environmental studies of infection since 2003 SARS epidemics, our team immediately explored our long-held hypothesis that short-range inhalation transmission might predominately the spread of most respiratory infection.
16:00-17:45
Novelty of the project
1. Our work provided the essential probable evidence for recognizing the airborne transmission of SARS-CoV-2.
2. We identified the chimney effect in the drainage stack explained more than 10 vertical COVID-19 outbreaks in Hong Kong.
3. Novel concept of inhalation transmission of SARS-CoV-2, which has been recognized by World Health Organization (WHO) and U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
4. Modified transmission routes as inhalation, spray and touch, which has been accepted by US CDC.
Benefit to the community
1. Recognition of airborne transmission paves the way for improving ventilation, e.g., in dine-in restaurants in Hong Kong, and for specifying maximum classroom capacity for each of HKU classrooms.
2. New concept of airborne transmission data for the need of wearing N95 masks by health care workers.
3. Novel concept of vertical outbreaks shows the urgent need for improving and monitoring drainage systems in high-rise houses.
4. The new concepts of aerosol inhalation, drop spray and surface touch promises easy communication for infection control of respiratory infection.
Achievement of the project
Professor Yuguo Li received one Medal of Honour, and 13 post-docs and students were on the list of Chief Executive's Commendation for Community Service. Their work was published in Annals of internal Medicine, Journal of Hazardous Materials etc.

Light-controlled Contamination-free Fluidic Processor
Professor Lijiu WANG
Chair Professor
Department of Mechanical Engineering
The fluidic processor resembles a "magic" optical hand that can navigate, fuse, pinch and cleave fluids in [unreadable] manner.
Fluid placed on the device beads up like a marble and neatly rolls without residue. By illuminating laser on the platform, a wavy force field is generated, acting as an invisible hand to touch and manipulate fluid.
Novelty of the project
A major breakthrough was that the processor is only 0.5% of that of the available technology. We consumed US$20 billion of plastics annually to handle fluids because of inter-sample contamination caused by [unreadable] The fluidic processor will drastically reduce disposable plastics and ease environmental strain.
A new world record: The device can manipulate the main liquid volume in the chemical industry its maneuverable fluid volume can be from 1000 µl to tiny droplets at 5000 µl, i.e. also able to move a mosquito drop in a mosquito bite which is 100 times smaller than that manipulated by its electrical counterpart.
Toward commercial products: The key technology of the device is a three-layer photo-responsive platform costing only about US$30 with a thickness of only [unreadable] it is portable and easy to handle.
Benefits to the community
Similar to a scenario in fantasy films where wizards levitate and move object around by raising their wands. The device can manipulate water, oil, milk, blood, ink, alcohol, also nanostructures and uses light as wand to move objects. This technology enables remote and contactless fluid processing is highly valuable for curbing the spread of infectious diseases and personal safety in facing testing of infectious viruses and bacteria.
Achievement of the project
The new technology has been published in Science Advances in an article titled "Photophysoelectric MicroFluidics", co-authored by Dr Wei LI, Dr Xin Tang and Chair Professor Lijiu Wang. It has been filed as US patent and received a GOLD award in the Geneva Inventions 2021.

TEXT:
Direct Thermal Charging Cell
Dr Tony S.P. FENG
Associate Professor
Department of Mechanical Engineering
Low-grade heat, which is abundantly available in the environment and even in human body, is always wasted without use.
Direct Thermal Charging Cell (DTCC) is invented for efficient heat-to-electricity conversion yielding a conversion efficiency over 5%, which surpasses all existing thermo-electrochemical and thermo-electric systems in low-grade heat regime.
Novelty of the project
DITCC can continuously convert heat to electricity under isothermal heating during the entire charge/discharge process and can be self-regenerated when cooled down. The synergistic chemical regeneration mechanism allows the device cyclicity. This is the first demonstration of a novel direct thermal charging cell (DTCC) that can achieve high efficiency in low-grade heat regime.
Benefit to the community
Low-grade heat recovery is a great challenge but also a promising opportunity to hike up energy conversion.
DITCC, with its excellent heat-to-electricity efficiency and advantages for practical application, can be applied in various fields such as HVAC, smart window and self-powered/wearable technologies. This project aims at reducing greenhouse effects. By establishing the startup and collaborating with industries, the innovation will bring about new applications, such as HVAC, smart window and self-powered/wearable technologies.
Achievement of the project
Award: Business Start-Up Award and Energy Award, Chemi Global Awards
Gold Medal, Top 10 Best Invention Award, 5th International Invention Innovation Competition, Hong Kong
Paper: Direct Thermal Charging Cell for Converting Low-grade Heat to Electricity, Nature Communications, 10, 489, 2019.
Patent: US Appl. 63/078764, PCT/CN2016/07777 TW 201955723.

TEXT:
Soft Magnetic Skin for Super-Resolution Tactile Sensing with Force Self-decoupling
Dr Jia PAN
Assistant Professor
Department of Computer Science
Human skin can sense subtle changes of both normal and shear forces as well as perceptive stimulus with finer resolution than the average spacing between mechanoreceptors. By contrast, existing tactile sensors for robotic applications are inferior, lacking both accurate force decoupling and proper spatial resolution. This project aims at developing skin-alike soft tactile sensors based on principles of magnetic fields.
Novelty of the project
In this project, we demonstrate a soft tactile sensor with self-decoupling and super-resolution abilities by designing a sinusoidally magnetized film as the sensing element. The sensor can accurately measure both normal force and shear force with a single unit and achieve a 60-fold increase in spatial resolution compared to existing tactile sensors.
Benefits to the community
This research provides new insight into tactile sensor design and could be beneficial to various applications in robotics field, such as adaptive grasping, delicate manipulation, and human-robot interaction.

Industry 4.0 Cases for Smart Manufacturing, Logistics,
and Construction
Professor George G.Q. HUANG
Chair Professor
Department of Industrial and
Manufacturing Systems Engineering
The housing shortage is a well-recognized challenge in Hong Kong.
To meet the huge and growing needs, productivity and
on-time delivery facilitated by modern building technology and decision support platforms in housing projects are crucial.
Besides, e-commerce has grown very fast recently. Professor Huang's team developed cyber-physical systems including both hardware and software solutions for construction and e-commerce logistics industries.
Novelty of the project
The solutions are deployed as cloud platforms for multiple stakeholders to use the corresponding services and eventually realize Industrial 4.0.
The key features include:
1. Since the real-time manufacturing and logistics data are captured using advanced ubiquitous devices, more efficient cross-border logistic and supply chain management can be achieved.
2. Real-time information traceability, visibility and interoperability tools integrate and interact with existing information systems, and achieve the seamless communication and coordination among multiple stakeholders throughout the project/logistics lifecycle.
3. It achieves better coordination for intralogistics within factories and warehouses, and city logistics for Just-in-Time (JIT) housing production.
Benefit to the community
Stakeholders use apps and IoT wearables to collect real-time information and build up a comprehensive view of the supply chain. The platform provides real-time statuses during manufacturing, logistics, warehouse or construction site. The use of the platform helps stakeholders to make better decisions in their daily operations.
Electronic data integration between different stakeholders reduces time for seamless information exchange, avoids information fragmentation, and helps to eliminate information blind spots.
Achievement of the project
With the support of Innovation and Technology Fund, solutions have been implemented in some building construction projects for Hong Kong Housing Authority and Hong Kong Property Services Department. The team got the award at ECSA 2018 for the iPark project.
The team also works with over 50 companies in Hong Kong and Mainland China for the iPark project.

Intelligent Mobile Robots for UVC based Disinfection
Professor Ning Xi
Chair Professor
Department of Industrial and Manufacturing Systems Engineering
Current surface disinfection methods include spraying chemicals or using UV light. However, it is difficult to directly spray liquid chemicals on surfaces due to the threat of negative environmental impacts and possible damage and contamination to various surfaces such as books and food packages. Currently, UV based disinfection lights are either wall mounted or operate on mobile bases. Moreover, they are often positioned metres away from surfaces that require disinfection.
Novelty of the project
The disinfection robot was developed based on the results of multi-year R&D on automatic robot programming, autonomous navigation and other related technologies. The UV surface disinfection robot provides a convenient and cost-effective solution to fight against the pandemic.
Benefit to the community
COVID-19 has been devastating on a global scale, and therefore preventing its spread is an essential step towards suppressing the virus. Many studies show that germs can remain viable for days or even weeks on many surfaces. Moreover, the COVID-19 virus can be viable for a number of days on many surfaces. Therefore, it is important to ensure that public facilities such as public libraries, restrooms, sports arenas, and other places are disinfected effectively.

TEXT:
HINCare: An Intelligent Timebanking System for Elderly Care
Professor Reynold C.K. CHENG
Professor Department of Computer Science
More than 20% of the population in Hong Kong will have an age of 65 or more by 2037.
It is important to encourage more helpers, who can be elders themselves, to help others voluntarily.
This will not only alleviate the shortage of helpers required for elderly care services,
but also enables "healthy ageing" and establishes a "mutual-help" culture.
A Metropolitan Information Network (MINT) for elder-helper relationship modeling
Novelty of the project
HINCare is the first intelligent system that enables timebanking for multiple NGOs in Hong Kong.
Traditional timebanking systems are designed to support one-to-one matching between helpers and elders,
while HINCare uses a novel MINT and AI technologies to perform helper-elder matching.
While most existing solutions support a single NGO, HINCare is the first system that supports multiple NGOs.
The project also includes a database for storing the relationship information of elderly people, helpers, and NGOs
and will be used by gerontology researchers and policymakers to extract insights about social behaviors,
thereby making better decisions.
Benefit to the community

TEXT:
Detection and Diagnostics of Airborne Viruses
Professor Anderson H.C. SHUM
Professor
Department of Mechanical Engineering
A lot of diseases can be transmitted via airborne agents, such as viruses spreading through droplets. The concentrations of these airborne agents are usually too low in the environment and it has created difficulties for the current detection instruments available in the market. We aim to fill this gap by developing new technologies to enhance detection and diagnostics of airborne viruses.
The development of new devices and instrumentations is based on a novel principle that can (1) detect airborne agents at lower virus concentration, and (2) identify the viruses in a short period of time.
In the future, zero contact with aerosols could be done during the virus detection process. This will not only improve the protection for medical staff but also alleviates the discomfort of participants during the test.
Benefit to the community
Airborne agents can be demonstrated to spread quickly in indoor environments. Our techniques can be potentially developed into instruments for environmental monitoring and early warning systems. The development of such instruments is timely, and these instruments can be deployed and distributed in indoor environments to alert the occupants about the presence of airborne agents. This will allow for the identification of potential group of infected persons and the control of spread of diseases.
It hopefully will help contribute to addressing future pandemics.
About the Centre
Advanced Biomedical Instrumentation Centre, set up with the funding support from the Health@InnoHK initiative by the Innovation and Technology Commission of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The Centre is a collaboration between HKU and the School of Engineering and Medicine at the University of California San Francisco (UCSF). The research and development themes include (1) Novel Therapeutic Approaches, (2) Advanced Medical Device Components, (3) Strategic Therapeutic Approaches, and (4) Advanced Medical Device Components.

The capstone project team will develop a universal testing machine specifically for soft and biomaterials with the minimal scale and production cost, such that in order to increase the availability of the universal testing machine, and enhancing the development and research on the new biomaterials. TEXT:
BazaAR - Augmented reality in Retail
typ18064
Anchit Sam
Archishma Verma
Dr. HF Ting
The Problem
The retail market in Hong Kong is dominated by three main types.
Physical stores, Online Stores and Hawkers.
Owing to Hong Kong's high rentals, retailers find it very expensive to set up physical stores.
Hawking industry on the other hand provides livelihood to more than 13000 people, but is likely to die soon due to government rules and regulations.
71% customers would shop at retailer more if they offered augmented reality as it would give them a chance to make sound shopping decisions
Our Solution
An all new intuitive shopping experience where hawkers can create 3D models of their products just by clicking photographs and display them in Augmented Reality for potential buyers to see and interact with.
B
BAZAAR
Bringing shops closer to you
A retail application that uses Augmented Reality and Photogrammetry
Features
Create detailed 3D models
Interaction in Augmented Reality
Friendly User Interface
The application provides an interface for shopkeepers to upload several pictures of there product, which would be modelled using photogrammetry to create detailed 3D models.
The 3D models would be spawned using AR for the user to place in his/her room setting. They would be able to visualise it accurately so as to make a sound purchasing decision
The UI serves as a platform between shopkeepers and customers which is as easy to use as any other e-commerce application
Technical Pipeline
model creation
Shopkeeper uploads images of product with their own camera using BSImage Picker ->
Rest calls to ReCAP API using Alamofire ->
Server sends a 3D model in the form of a URL -> URL added to the backend database ->
object spawning
Customer browses through various products on the application ->
When he/she selects a product, a 3D model is pulled from the database ->
3D model is spawned using ARKit ->
User Interacts with the 3D model by scaling and rotating ->
User makes a sound purchasing decision

SMART OZONE STERILIZING ROBOT
Ozone is the most efficient disinfectant against all types of microorganisms.

All the structures macromolecular cells are altered, decomposed and disappeared due to its high capacity for direct oxidation.
CLOUD
Our cloud platform is built by ASPNet and is made for two purposes. First: for ozone concentration tracking. Air quality inside the sterilization room can be monitored to ensure that it is safe enough for humans to get in. Second: for robot location tracking, we can have real-time tracking of a robot during product delivery to avoid off-tracking and losing.
ROS
Robot Operating System-ROS. ROS is more like a framework responsible for communicating and operating the various components of the robot. Take the walking of the robot as an example. To make the robot walk, it needs to control the motor underneath, and there are some obstacle avoidance sensors. The functions in ROS act like a bridge for the controlling programs of both motors and the sensors to communicate and coordinate.
AGV
Agv means automated guided vehicle which can follow the wires on the floor. Our purchased agv can be controlled by ROS language and it has vision camera for navigation. We would set the route for the agv to fit the layout of the elderly home. To avoid the collision between the agv and the elderslies, our agv will design with highly maneuverable with suitable size and moving speed.

IDEAS AND AIDS
The ACSS aims to reduce man power needed in preparation work of conference seats. It is started in 2019 by Innowing and now it is at the phase II. The structure is separated into three moveable parts, designing for the simplest amount of motions needed for transporting the chair. The electrical part is also kept as simple as possible for smoother and safer operation.
ROBOTIC ARM STRUCTURE
The transportation of chair heavily depends on robotic arm, so we need a robotic arm with high durability and strength to overcome the deflection and weight of chair during operation.
SEPARATING MECHANISM
The separators aim at overcoming the pressure between chairs to separate them from a column. The separators are made using 3D printer and installed in the middle of the clamp. TEXT:
>> MediDrop: Delivery of Medical Equipment with Drones
WE'RE LOOKING FOR MORE TEAM MEMBERS!
> Introduction <
Our project seeks to alleviate some of the health threats in Southeast Asia due to limited access to roads and healthcare facilities. It suggests the use of drones to deliver medical supplies. The design of our drone service differs from existing companies because it proposes larger service areas, incorporates the idea of a telemedicine service to reduce the need to travel for medical consultation, focuses on a supplier-to-patient network structure rather than a supplier-to-hospital network structure, and suggests using public health centers or small clinics as delivery centers if patients do not have access to phone or internet.
> Technology <
Our current prototype involves a latching mechanism that uses a servo motor to grab the box in place, securely and safely. Our prototype will be able to catch and release the load from our base station to a set point with or without supervision. With more funding, we will investigate and experiment new forms of loading mechanisms as well as other drone technologies to ensure a more reliable and smooth delivery.
With the rise of 5G and AI, we can form a network of drones to deliver medicine to communities that need it quickly. In the case of a pandemic such as the current COVID-19 pandemic, our drones can potentially deliver cold storage containers for these vaccines
> Plan of Action <
Once our drones and latching mechanism have been designed and successfully tested, we are hoping to implement this project in parts of Southeast Asia that are particularly disadvantaged in terms of access to roads and medical services. Specifically, we have identified the regions of Ratanak Kiri in Cambodia, and West Kalimantan and Riau in Indonesia as potential implementation areas. In this later phase of the project, we will seek to work with local governments to obtain the necessary permissions to operate our drones (e.g., commercial licenses for drone use) and help deliver medical supplies. We are currently focusing on securing sources of funding for this later phases of the project. In particular, we will be applying to the Gallant Ho Experiential Learning Fund, as well as funding from the Tam Wing Innovation Wing.

Survival guide for COVID-19: Why ventilation matters?
Although airborne transmission of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has already been acknowledged by leading health authorities, no existing standard for building ventilation yet considers the need to control respiratory infection. The speaker shall explain why outdoor has a lower infection risk than indoor, and why poor ventilation can worsen both short- and long-range inhalation. The speaker shall present a new equal CO2 exposure method to derive a set of minimum ventilation rates and associated maximum CO2 concentrations in indoor settings with various activity levels (rest, light-, moderate- and heavy-exercise) and breathing modes (breathing, speaking, singing and loudly speaking). Opportunities for innovation will be mentioned.

Robot Operating System (ROS)
to build robot applications
The Robot Operating System (ROS) is a set of software libraries and tools that help you build robot applications. From drivers to state-of-the-art algorithms, and with powerful developer tools, ROS has what you need for your next robotics project and it is important to everyone who wants to work in the field of robotics.
Robot Control - Firmware
to control the actuators of a robot
Firmware is software program in MCU (micro controller unit) to control the actuators such as servos and motors, and sensors of a robot. It is a challenge to coordinate each module (sensor or actuator) in the robot efficiently to avoid one module blocking another which causing serious consequence.

to design and create 3D modelling contents

HKU DEPARTMENT OF INDUSTRIAL AND MANUFACTURING SYSTEMS ENGINEERING
SMART OZONE STERILIZING ROBOT
Ozone is the most efficient disinfectant against all types of microorganisms.
It is effective in eliminating virus, fungi and bacteria.
All the structures macromolecular cells are altered, decomposed and disappeared due to its high capacity for direct oxidation.
CLOUD
Our cloud platform is built by ASPNet and is made for two purposes. First: for ozone concentration tracking. Air quality inside the sterilization room can be monitored to ensure that it is safe enough for humans to get in. Second: for robot location tracking, we can have real-time tracking of a robot during product delivery to avoid off-tracking and losing.
ROS
Robot Operating System-ROS. ROS is more like a framework responsible for communicating and operating the various components of the robot. Take the walking of the robot as an example. To make the robot walk, it needs to control the motor underneath, and there are some obstacle avoidance sensors. The functions in ROS act like a bridge for the controlling programs of both motors and the sensors to communicate and coordinate.
AGV
Agv means automated guided vehicle which can follow the wires on the floor. Our purchased agv can be controlled by ROS language and it has vision camera for navigation. We would set the route for the agv to fit the layout of the elderly home. To avoid the collision between the agv and the elderslies, our agv will design with highly maneuverable with suitable size and moving speed.

POINEER
HKU DEPARTMENT OF INDUSTRIAL AND MANUFACTURING SYSTEMS ENGINEERING
SMART OZONE STERILIZING ROBOT
Ozone is the most efficient disinfectant against all types of microorganisms.
It is effective in eliminating virus, fungi and bacteria.
All the structures macromolecular cells are altered, decomposed and disappeared due to its high capacity for direct oxidation.
CLOUD
Our cloud platform is built by ASPNet and is made for two purposes. First: for ozone concentration tracking. Air quality inside the sterilization room can be monitored to ensure that it is safe enough for humans to get in. Second: for robot location tracking, we can have real-time tracking of a robot during product delivery to avoid off-tracking and losing.
ROS
Robot Operating System-ROS. ROS is more like a framework responsible for communicating and operating the various components of the robot. Take the walking of the robot as an example. To make the robot walk, it needs to control the motor underneath, and there are some obstacle avoidance sensors. The functions in ROS act like a bridge for the controlling programs of both motors and the sensors to communicate and coordinate.
AGV
Agv means automated guided vehicle which can follow the wires on the floor. Our purchased agv can be controlled by ROS language and it has vision camera for navigation. We would set the route for the agv to fit the layout of the elderly home. To avoid the collision between the agv and the elderslies, our agv will design with highly maneuverable with suitable size and moving speed.

Lumino in a Nutshell
Technological advancements are not uncommon in the past decades. However, navigation remains a challenge for the visually impaired till this day and age. With Lumino, we are tackling this issue with a new approach.
Existing Solutions
Costly
• Existing solutions are pricey and hence unaffordable for many.
Crumbled
• Interview results revealed that existing solutions fail to address the basic needs of the visually impaired.
Lack Functionality
• Simple solutions lack the functionality needed to enhance the daily lives of the visually impaired.
VS
Lumino
Solution
• Lumino is an all-in-one, innovative navigation solution affordable to all, giving the visually impaired their deserved freedom.

Costly

Crumbled

Lack Functionality

Solution

TEXT:
2-DAY BEGINNER WORKSHOP: ROBOT CONTROL — FIRMWARE
Firmware is the software program in MCU (micro controller unit) to control the actuators such as servos and motors, and sensors of a robot. It is a challenge to develop a good firmware as MCU is not powerful as computer CPU. As MCU program runs in single thread model, programming techniques are required to efficiently coordinate each module (sensor or actuator) to avoid them from blocking each other. In this two-day workshop, you will learn the essential knowledge on writing firmware and apply what you have learnt to write the firmware for a wheel driven robot - WheeBot.
HKU Engineering students and InnoHub members, preferably with C/C++ programming knowledge, are welcome to join.

TEXT:

Faculty of Engineering, HKU
Innovations in studying the past with technology
Technology is increasingly important in studying humanities topics such as archaeology.
For example, when we study the materials left behind by the past societies, such as their architecture, pottery or animal bones from meals, the complex data are digitalized to capture information about the space, shape, decoration and materials to facilitate our study of the human past.
HKU helps lead a collaborative fieldwork project in Armenia every summer where we are excavating a fortress from 3000 years ago. This field project is a laboratory for experimenting with various technologies including drone-based Lidar, 3D scanning of spaces and objects, computer vision, machine learning databases and many other technologies, in the hot and dusty field conditions.
In this workshop, we will introduce some of the past engineering experiments and their technological difficulties. All participants can join us in developing new technological solutions that can facilitate our field works in the future. Participating students may also get a chance to join us in Armenia next summer!
Speaker:
Dr Peter Cobb
Assistant Professor, School of Humanities, HKU
Dr Cobb teaches courses on archaeological methods and theories and the archaeology of the ancient world, including experiential learning classes abroad. He has conducted archaeological fieldwork in Laos, Armenia, and Turkey. He is currently involved with the Armenian Solar Panel Archaeological Project (ASAP) in collaboration with the Armenian Institute of Archaeology and Ethnography. His research focuses on the Late Bronze and Iron Age societies of the Near East, especially those in modern Southwest Asia (aka the Ancient Near East). Dr Cobb is a specialist in the analysis of ancient ceramics and in digital humanities (DH). He holds a joint appointment with the Human Communication Development, and Information Sciences academic unit of the Faculty of Education.

TEXT:
Innovation Academy
Faculty of Engineering, HKU
ONLINE WORKSHOP
From hospital-centric to human-centric:
Personalized wearables For digital healthcare
The soaring population aging, the quarantine and the shortage of medical instrumentations are demanding decentralized medical technologies that can enable remote and personalized healthcare. Wearable technologies are the protagonists. Emerging wearable devices include, but are not limited to, smartwatches, smart clothing, smart glasses, smart jewelry, and wearable cameras. Some of these wearables can already measure vital signals such as heart rates, breathing rates and blood pressure. Moving forward, next-generation wearables are expected to enable on-demand blood tests and continuous recording of our electrophysiological signals for disease screening and monitoring. However, several challenges remain.
In this workshop, the speaker will describe how wearable technologies are impacting our healthcare systems, how to develop a wearable device, how we can address the most pressing challenges with transdisciplinary biomedical engineering approaches, and finally, how Biomedical Engineering can ultimately improve the human health.
Speaker:
Dr Shiming Zhang
Dr Shiming Zhang is currently an Assistant Professor at the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) of the University of Hong Kong (HKU), leading the wearable, intelligent and soft electronics (WISE) research group. He has ten years' research experience in developing wearable technologies for human-centric and personalized healthcare. Some of these technologies have been commercialized by a startup company. He has authored/co-authored about 50 journal and conference articles in the field of wearables and co-founded the startup company SESIC, which aims to develop wearable medical devices. He has received many awards, including the title of Vanier Canada Scholar by the Government of Canada, and the Chinese Government Award for Outstanding Student Abroad.

TEXT: Innovation Academy Faculty of Engineering, HKU ONLINE WORKSHOP Crafting the multiverse of cells to reshape healthcare In the past 10 years at HKU Engineering, Professor Kevin Tsia and his team have developed a suite of optical imaging technologies that generated brand new views and understanding of the living biological cells. They include: capturing high-resolution motion picture of the swift-flying brain signals; visualising the inner workings of cells and organisms in 3D; and detecting rare cancer cells in millions of blood cells. In this workshop, Professor Tsia will describe how and why these technologies, when cautiously synergised with artificial intelligence, can be used for generating and analyzing all the unprecedented data relevant to the millions and millions of cells. It is essentially to create a “multiverse” of cells from which we could unlock the previously unknown information for supporting new biological discovery, and new-generation of cost-effective clinical diagnosis.
Kevin Tsia is currently a Professor in the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering and the Program Director of the Biomedical Engineering Program at the University of Hong Kong. His research interest covers a broad range of subject matters including ultra-fast optical imaging for imaging flow cytometry and high-speed in-vivo brain imaging, bioinformatics approaches for single-cell analysis. He is currently the HK Research Grants Council (RGC) Research Fellow (2020). He received Early Career Award 2012-2013 by RGC in Hong Kong. He also received the Outstanding Young Research Award 2015 at HKU as well as 14th Chinese Science and Technology Award for Young Scientists in 2016. He is author or coauthor of over 200 journal publications conference papers and book chapters.
